title: Consider IpAddr for the group argument of UDP multicast join methods
body:
Should `UdpServer::join_multicast_group` (IPv4) and `UdpServer::join_multicast_group_v6` take an `IpAddr` for the multicast group?

Both methods currently require an `Addr` (IP and port). Their documentation says membership only uses the IP. The receive port is set when the socket is bound. For example, a server bound to port 9000 can be passed a group address ending in port 5353, even though the call still receives multicast traffic on port 9000. The existing multicast test copies the server port into the group address just to call the join method.

Consider narrowing the group parameter on both methods to `IpAddr`. A caller holding an endpoint would migrate as follows:

```diff
- server.join_multicast_group(endpoint, interface_addr~)
+ server.join_multicast_group(endpoint.ip, interface_addr~)
```

This is a source-breaking signature change for direct callers and typed method references. The design decision for 1.0 is whether the clearer type warrants that migration. The bind constructor still needs a port, and the IPv4 and IPv6 interface-selection arguments serve a separate purpose.

[IPv4 membership](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/blob/57464f4ec/async/socket/udp.mbt#L365-L399) · [IPv6 membership](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/blob/57464f4ec/async/socket/udp.mbt#L403-L436) · [Existing call site](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/blob/57464f4ec/async/socket/multicast_test.mbt#L54-L61)

title: Mark Directory::remove as nocancel so it can be used in task cleanup
perf: incremental flate encoder performs unnecessary output copy
body:
The current incremental DEFLATE encoder first writes each completed block into the growable `BitWriter.out` array. `IncrementalEncoder::drain_output` then copies those compressed bytes into the caller's `MutArrayView[Byte]`. This extra layer is what permits arbitrary output sizes, including zero or one byte, without making block emission resumable, but every compressed byte takes an additional copy.

One possible optimization is a direct-output bit writer with resumable block emission. In the common path, block headers and tokens are written directly to the caller's output view. When that view ends mid-emission, the encoder retains the bit accumulator, emission phase, and token index; alternatively, it may finish only the current bounded token into a small spill buffer and drain that first on the next call.

This removes the block-sized compressed-output array and copy while preserving one-byte output support. Dynamic Huffman encoding still needs bounded block planning state—principally the token array and frequency tables—but that state describes input decisions and is independent of compressed-output buffering.

title: Proposal: staged, machine-fixable deprecations for large API migrations
body:
## Summary

Core needs to make some API changes that are too big to do with today's `#deprecated`. The clearest case is `length()` → `len()`, which #975 already decided on. Today a deprecation either warns loudly, which breaks every `--deny-warn` build at once, or it doesn't happen. This proposal adds three pieces that together make a large rename gradual and mostly automatic:

1. **Structured replacements on `#deprecated`.** The compiler gets the exact rewrite, not just a prose message, so each warning carries an edit that can be applied mechanically.
2. **A quiet `soft` level** (name open, see below). It's off by default, shown in `moon test` output and as an editor hint, and never counted by `--deny-warn` unless a package opts in.
3. **`moon fix`.** It applies the compiler's edits across all targets. Sites that can't be rewritten mechanically go into a machine-readable report, for a person or an AI agent to finish.

Core is where most of these migrations start and the biggest user of them, so the proposal is filed here. Pieces 1 and 2 need compiler work and piece 3 needs `moon` work. Once the design is agreed, they can be split into issues in those repos.

## Motivation

### 1. `length` → `len` is decided but blocked

#975 settled the naming question in April 2025. The decision there was to unify on `len` for both `length` and `size`, matching Rust, to keep `length` for the time being, and to provide a migration tool for `length` later. `Map::size` and `Set::size` have since been folded into `length`. The `length` → `len` step itself hasn't happened, and no migration tool exists yet: `moon` 0.1.20261104 has no `fix` command.

How big it is, measured on `main`:

| | count |
|---|---|
| public types with a `length()` method | 30 (`Array`, `FixedArray`, `String`, `StringView`, `Bytes`, `BytesView`, `Map`, `HashMap`, `Deque`, `Queue`, `List`, `Buffer`, …) |
| `.length()` call sites in core | ~4,800 |
| files containing them | 615 |

That's core alone. Every downstream package and every doc example adds to it.

A text substitution can't do this rename safely. `.length()` on a user-defined type that has nothing to do with core has to stay as it is. The rewrite has to be **type-directed**, and only the compiler knows the receiver's type.

### 2. Label cleanups have the same shape, at a smaller scale

The pre-1.0 label cleanups (#4613, #4626) rename labels one PR at a time, for example `Bytes::to_unchecked_string(length?)` → `len?` in #4801. `#label_migration(new, alias=old)` already records the exact rewrite, so these are mechanically fixable today. What's missing is a tool that applies them, and a way to ship them without warning every user at once.

### 3. Most existing deprecation messages can't be acted on by a tool

On `main`, core has **785** `#deprecated` attributes and **37** `#label_migration` attributes. Leaving out the 442 trait-method promotions in `extends.mbt`, the remaining **344** look like this:

| shape | approx. count | mechanically fixable? |
|---|---|---|
| no message at all | 106 | no: the tool doesn't even know what to suggest |
| plain rename (``"Use `foo` instead"``) or operator (``"Use `!=` instead"``) | ~70 | yes, **if** the target were structured instead of prose |
| prose needing judgement (semantics change, different signature, "see README") | ~170 | no: needs a person or an AI |

(Rough classification by regex over the messages.)

Even the easy third is locked in free text. A tool could guess at ``"Use `foo` instead"``, but guessing at rewrites isn't acceptable for a compiler-backed fix.

## Proposal

The syntax below shows the idea only. The exact attribute grammar is for the compiler team to decide.

### Part 1: structured replacements

```moonbit
#deprecated("Use `len` instead", replacement="len")
pub fn[T] Array::length(self : Array[T]) -> Int { self.len() }
```

- `replacement=` names the new item: a method or function in the same namespace, a path like `@pkg.name`, or an operator for the `op_*` derivatives.
- The compiler resolves each use **with type information** and attaches an exact, machine-applicable edit to the warning, as `rustc` does for `cargo fix`.
- `#label_migration` already has this information. It just needs to emit an edit too.
- Deprecations with no structured replacement keep their message and get no edit. This part is purely additive.

### Part 2: a `soft` level

```moonbit
#deprecated("Use `len` instead", replacement="len", level=soft)
```

| | `level=soft` | default (today's) |
|---|---|---|
| `moon check` / `moon build` | silent | warning |
| `--deny-warn` | **not counted** | error |
| `moon test` | listed in an end-of-run summary, never fails | warning |
| IDE | hint plus quick fix | warning plus quick fix |
| opt in per package | through the warning settings in `moon.pkg` | n/a |

Python's experience is the reason for the `moon test` row. `PendingDeprecationWarning` is ignored at runtime, and the place developers actually see it is the test runner: `unittest` re-enables warnings, and pytest lists them in its summary. A soft warning that's silent everywhere is a warning nobody sees.

A soft deprecation is meant to be **staged**, not permanent:

```
soft (release N)  →  default warning (N + k)  →  removed (pre-1.0) / kept hidden
```

Optionally the attribute records the planned stage, for example `escalate_after="0.x"`, so the move to a louder warning is tracked rather than forgotten. Without a planned stage, a soft deprecation becomes two spellings forever. #4698 ("Live duplicate aliases") already lists that as a problem.

Docs and the generated `.mbti` show only the preferred name, the same treatment as `#doc(hidden)`, so the interface doesn't list both.

### Part 3: `moon fix`

```bash
moon fix --dry-run          # show the diff
moon fix                    # apply edits, then run moon fmt
moon fix --only soft        # or: --only label-migration, --only deprecated
moon fix --report json      # sites that have no mechanical edit
```

- **All targets.** Core has target-specific files, for example `bigint_js.mbt`, `bigint_wide.mbt` and `bigint_default.mbt`. A fix run for one target would miss the others, so `moon fix` checks every target, like `moon check --target all`, and merges the edits.
- **Your own code only.** It never edits dependencies.
- **Runs `moon fmt` afterward**, because renames change line widths. #4801's tests collapsed an `assert_eq` onto one line this way.
- **Reports what it can't fix.** For each remaining site, `--report json` gives the location, the deprecated item, its message and its target. That's exactly what a person, or an AI agent, needs to finish the job.

## Where AI fits

`moon fix` doesn't need AI, and its core shouldn't use it.

- **Mechanical renames are better done deterministically.** `length` → `len`, label renames and `op_lt` → `<` are exact given type information. A deterministic edit is reproducible, can be reviewed as a plain diff, and is safe to run in CI. `cargo fix`, `go fix` and `dart fix` all work this way.
- **AI is for the judgement third.** For example `BigInt::to_octets` → `to_be_bytes`, `Show` → `@debug.Debug`, or helpers that changed meaning. A rename can't express those. Here the `--report json` output is the interface: an agent reads each site with its message and the surrounding code and proposes a change, and a person reviews it. Today core's pre-1.0 migrations find their call sites by grepping, one PR at a time. A structured report would make that faster and less error-prone.
- **Good deprecation messages help both.** A `migration=` link or a longer note on the hard cases is useful to people and to models.

So `moon fix` is not too hard to build without AI. Compiler-provided edits are the hard part, and that's what Part 1 adds.

## Worked example: `length` → `len`

1. Core adds `len()` next to `length()` on all 30 types and marks `length` `#deprecated(..., replacement="len", level=soft)`.
2. Core runs `moon fix` on itself. All ~4,800 call sites are rewritten in one reviewable PR.
3. Downstream users see nothing until they run `moon test`, or they opt in, or their editor shows the hint. Then `moon fix` migrates them in one command.
4. After the agreed period, `length` moves to the default level, and later it's removed or hidden.

The same flow applies to the remaining `length` labels (`BigInt::to_octets(length?)`, `@random.shuffle(length~)`) and to the label cleanups in #4626.

## Non-goals

- Changing any API in this issue. `length` → `len` is the motivating example, and #975 owns that decision.
- Rewriting dependencies or published packages.
- Using AI inside `moon fix` itself.

## Open questions

1. **Name of the level.** `soft`, `preferred`, `pending` or `hint`?
2. **`moon test` visibility.** Should soft warnings be summarized in `moon test` by default (the pytest model), or only with a flag?
3. **Trait methods.** If a deprecated method is also a trait method, or user code implements a trait whose method is being renamed, what does the edit do?
4. **Staging metadata.** Should the escalation release be recorded in the attribute, or tracked only in issues?
5. **Scope of `replacement=`.** Renames and operators only, or simple argument reshaping too (for example dropping a label)?

## Related

- #975: naming decision to unify on `len`, migration tool promised
- #4613, #4626: pre-1.0 label cleanups (`len` for slices)
- #4698: live duplicate aliases (why soft deprecations need an end date)
- #4801: example label migration (`to_unchecked_string(length?)` → `len?`)

title: [wasm/wasm-gc] Int and Int64 division overflow (min_value / -1) aborts instead of wrapping
body:
Summary
On the wasm and wasm-gc backends, integer division overflow aborts the program:
RuntimeError: divide result unrepresentable
On js, the same expression evaluates to -2147483648 and execution continues normally.
The same divergence exists for Int64.
moonbitlang/core documents Int as a 32-bit two's-complement type whose operations wrap
around on overflow, so the two wasm backends appear to diverge from that documented behaviour.
If trapping is the intended semantics instead, then the behaviour is currently undocumented
and inconsistent across backends — either way it would be worth pinning down.
Environment
- moon 0.1.20261020 (2284bd2 2026-10-20)
- moonc v0.10.16+b1a0e846e (2026-10-16)
- moonbitlang/core 0.10.16
- Windows 11 (10.0.26100), x86_64
- Node.js v22.22.2
- Backends tested: wasm, wasm-gc, js
(native was not run locally — this machine has no MSVC Build Tools)
Minimal reproduction
No dependencies, 7 lines:
fn main {
  let a : Int = -2147483648
  let b : Int = -1
  println("before")
  println(a / b)
  println("after")
}
moon run main --target wasm:
before
RuntimeError: divide result unrepresentable
    at __moonbit_main
moon run main --target wasm-gc:
before
RuntimeError: divide result unrepresentable
    at __moonbit_main <repo>/main/main.mbt:5
In both cases after is never printed and the process exits with code 1:
the abort kills the whole program, it is not a catchable error value.
moon run main --target js:
before
-2147483648
after
It is not a constant-folding artifact. Taking the divisor from @env.args() at runtime
gives the same result on all three backends:
// moon.pkg: import { "moonbitlang/core/env" }
fn main {
  let args = @env.args()
  let b : Int = if args.length() > 0 { -1 } else { 1 }
  let a : Int = -2147483648
  println("before")
  println(a / b)
  println("after")
}
The same holds for Int64 (-9223372036854775807L - 1L divided by -1L):
wasm / wasm-gc raise the same RuntimeError, js returns -9223372036854775808.
What the documentation currently says
From core/builtin/intrinsics.mbt:
- Add for Int32: "Performs two's complement arithmetic, which means the operation will
wrap around if the result exceeds the range of a 32-bit integer." The doc example is
2147483647 + 1 == -2147483648.
- Div for Int32: documents truncation towards zero and "Throws a panic if divisor is zero".
It does not say what happens when the quotient itself is not representable.
So the wrapping rule is stated for arithmetic in general and demonstrated for addition,
but the division doc comment only covers the divisor-is-zero case.
Expected behaviour
If integer division follows the same wrapping rule as the rest of the fixed-width arithmetic,
then Int::min_value / -1 should be Int::min_value, and Int64::min_value / -1 should be
Int64::min_value — which is what the js backend already does.
If trapping is intentional, it would help to:
1. document it on Div for Int32 / Div for Int64 (the current doc only mentions division
by zero), and
2. decide what js should do, since it currently wraps silently.
How this was found
This came out of a cross-backend differential harness I maintain,
[MoonDiff](https://github.com/wuhaiting321/MoonDiff), which runs the same primitive operations
on all four backends and compares the results bit-for-bit. The three-instruction program is
checked in as examples/min-div-overflow.json.
I am happy to run extra probes, test native on Linux, or narrow this down further if that
would help.

title: Build the `@http` types on wasm-gc, and add constructors for `RequestHeader` and `ResponseHeader`
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

`moonbitlang/core/async/http` is not built on wasm-gc, so code that only uses its types (`RequestMethod`, `Headers`, `RequestHeader`, `ResponseHeader`, `Cookie`) cannot build there either. Some libraries keep their I/O-free code building on wasm-gc; see the comments below for examples.

`RequestHeader` and `ResponseHeader` are `pub(all)`, so code outside the package can build them with struct literals, and adding a field to them would break that code. `Cookie` already has read-only fields and a constructor.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

- Build `@http` on wasm-gc with only the types, as the JS backend builds only the client.
- Add constructors for `RequestHeader` and `ResponseHeader`, with default values for fields added later, so that the types can become read-only and gain fields without breaking their users.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Move the types to a separate package without I/O. This issue first proposed that; it was dropped in the discussion below, since the types are tied to other design choices of `@http`.

**Additional context**

This issue was originally titled "Move the HTTP types out of async/http before 1.0" and was narrowed after the discussion below.

- [x] I do think that this should be part of the core library and should be delivered to all the MoonBit developers.

async/fs: read_binary(sync_timestamp=true) fails with access denied on Windows
body:
## Problem

On Windows Native, `moonbitlang/core/async/fs.read_binary(path, sync_timestamp=true)` fails with “Access is denied” on a file that can otherwise be read and written. The default read succeeds, and explicitly opening the same file with `ReadWrite`, reading it, and calling `sync()` also succeeds.

The [API documentation and implementation](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/blob/main/async/fs/file.mbt) expose `sync_timestamp` (default `false`) and describe waiting for timestamp changes to reach the filesystem when it is enabled.

## Reproduction environment

- An actual Windows machine, run locally from PowerShell.
- Native debug target, built using Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools / MSVC.
- The probe imports the installed `moonbitlang/core/async/fs`; it does not copy its implementation.
- Diagnostic source: [ad654280c7214b400bde355211618a5b329c7964](https://github.com/ZSeanYves/x/tree/ad654280c7214b400bde355211618a5b329c7964/internal/sync_timestamp_probe).

## Steps to reproduce

With MoonBit and the Native C toolchain available:

```powershell
git clone --branch codex/repro-windows-sync-timestamp https://github.com/ZSeanYves/x.git sync-timestamp-repro
cd sync-timestamp-repro
git checkout ad654280c7214b400bde355211618a5b329c7964
moon test internal/sync_timestamp_probe --target native
```

The [test](https://github.com/ZSeanYves/x/blob/ad654280c7214b400bde355211618a5b329c7964/internal/sync_timestamp_probe/probe_test.mbt) creates a temporary file, exercises both core async and x/fs, checks the returned bytes, and removes the file afterward. The relevant core calls are:

```moonbit
// @async_fs = moonbitlang/core/async/fs
assert_eq(@async_fs.read_binary(path), data) // succeeds
assert_eq(
  @async_fs.read_binary(path, sync_timestamp=true),
  data,
) // fails on Windows

// Control, using the same file:
let file = @async_fs.open(path, mode=ReadWrite)
defer file.close()
assert_eq(file.read_all(), data)
file.sync() // succeeds
```

## Observed results

Relevant output from the Windows run:

```text
core_async.default: OK
core_async.sync_timestamp: @fs.read_binary(sync_timestamp=true): Access is denied.
core_async.read_write_sync: OK
win32.read_only_flush: 5
win32.read_write_flush: 0
Total tests: 1, passed: 0, failed: 1.
```

The [direct Win32 control](https://github.com/ZSeanYves/x/blob/ad654280c7214b400bde355211618a5b329c7964/internal/sync_timestamp_probe/probe.c) reports error 5 (`ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED`) when flushing a `GENERIC_READ` handle, and success with `GENERIC_READ | GENERIC_WRITE`. The file contents remain unchanged. The same MoonBit probe passes on macOS; the Win32-specific control is skipped there.

## Cause and coverage

`read_binary` opens the file with `ReadOnly`, reads it, then calls `fsync(only_data=false)` when `sync_timestamp=true`. The [Native runtime](https://github.com/moonbitlang/moonbit-native-runtime/blob/88e2a69ffff2f3faae07d2a94a9f7e54808cc2d1/fs.c) maps read-only access to `GENERIC_READ` and implements Windows synchronization using `FlushFileBuffers`. [Microsoft's documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-flushfilebuffers) requires the handle to have `GENERIC_WRITE` access.

`read_text(sync_timestamp=true)` has the same read-only-open / fsync sequence in the current source, so it appears affected too, but the Windows probe above directly tested `read_binary` only.

The existing [timestamp test](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/blob/main/async/fs/timestamp_test.mbt) returns early on Windows before exercising `read_text(sync_timestamp=true)`, so that test does not cover this failure.

## Expected behavior / question

Could we clarify the intended Windows contract for `sync_timestamp=true` and either support it or document the platform/access limitation explicitly?

Default reads (`sync_timestamp=false`) are unaffected and should retain read-only access. Unconditionally switching reads to `ReadWrite` would impose a new write-permission requirement, so this report does not prescribe that fix. A Windows regression test could check the opt-in operation's behavior without assuming that Windows updates access timestamps immediately.

title: async/fs: support opt-in newline normalization in read_text
body:
## Motivation

Text-processing scripts often need to handle both LF and CRLF files, especially when a repository is checked out on different operating systems. Splitting a CRLF file on `"\n"` leaves a trailing `"\r"` on each line. This can make anchored regular expressions for manifest versions or changelog headings fail unexpectedly.

We encountered this while migrating a Selene release script from Python to MoonBit and had to normalize newlines explicitly after decoding. This is a recurring text-file reading concern that could be handled consistently by the library.

The current [`async/fs.read_text`](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/blob/main/async/fs/file.mbt) delegates to the text reader, whose [`read_all`](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/blob/main/async/io/text_reader.mbt) decodes UTF-8 without newline normalization. A caller currently needs something like:

```moonbit
let text = @fs.read_text(path)
  .replace_all(old="\r\n", new="\n")
```

That workaround handles CRLF but does not cover standalone CR.

## Proposal

Add an optional parameter to `async/fs.read_text`, for example:

```moonbit
let text = @fs.read_text(path, normalize_newlines=true)
```

Suggested semantics:

- The default is `false`, preserving existing behavior and the file's original line endings.
- When enabled, normalize both CRLF (`"\r\n"`) and standalone CR (`"\r"`) to LF (`"\n"`). Existing LF is unchanged, and a CRLF pair produces exactly one LF.
- Do not add a missing final newline. Preserve the current UTF-8 decoding/error behavior and the existing parameters such as `sync_timestamp`.

For example, enabling normalization would convert `"a\r\nb\rc\nd"` to `"a\nb\nc\nd"`.

This corresponds to the input normalization performed by Python's [universal-newline text reading](https://docs.python.org/3/library/io.html#io.TextIOWrapper). The parameter name is a suggestion; an explicit newline-policy enum would also be reasonable if preferred.

Tests should cover LF, CRLF, standalone CR, mixed endings, empty input, input without a final newline, Unicode content, and unchanged default/error behavior.

[cross-package-23] Near-empty packages (new ones)
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **cross-package-23**, Part 2 (smaller API finding from the `cross-package` report). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**Near-empty packages (new ones)** (Low · API · breaking to fix: no)

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### cross-package-23 — Near-empty packages (new ones)
_Low · API · breaking to fix: no · from the [`cross-package` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620751625)_

- `path/error` (1 type, re-exported by `@path`), `async/types` (`Platform` + `type Fd = UInt64`, and `Fd` is unused — `File::fd() -> UInt64`), `async/signal` (1 enum + 1 fn), `async/os_error`, `async/cond_var`/`semaphore`/`aqueue` (5–9 items, re-exported by `@async`, so two import paths per type). `@tls.rand_bytes`/`sha1` are `#internal` helpers but public (duplicate `@env.rand`). fix: move `path/error` under `path/internal` (or into `path`), use `Fd` in signatures or drop it; keep the async split but document `@async.*` as the canonical path.
- Source: me.

## Notes for whoever picks this up

- **Re-check against `main` first.** The review ran at `0cf74cb9c` (2026-11-04); the code links below are pinned to that commit. If the problem is already gone, comment with the evidence and close as fixed.
- **Read [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/blob/main/AGENTS.md)**: the trait-method promotion (`extend`) policy, deprecated blocks go in `deprecated.mbt`, `moon info && moon fmt` at the end.
- **This is an API change, so the `.mbti` diff is the deliverable.** Prefer deprecate-then-remove: keep the old name as `#deprecated("use X")` pointing at the replacement. Put the before/after `.mbti` diff in the PR description.
- **Settled contracts — don't re-litigate:** Strings are valid UTF-16; `raise?` for eager non-mutating higher-order functions; `Json(x)` instead of `x.to_json()`.
- **If the right answer needs a maintainer decision** (naming, which semantics to keep), post the options with a recommendation as a comment here before writing a large patch.
- **Verify:** `moon check`, `moon test` on every target the package builds for (`--target native` for `async/*`), plus a test that pins the new behaviour.
- **PR text:** `Closes #<this issue>` and `Part of #4613 (cross-package-23)`. Don't write `Fixes #4613`; that would close the parent.

## Done when

- [ ] Decision recorded here (or the report's proposal accepted as-is)
- [ ] Change merged, or closed as won't fix with a one-line reason
- [ ] `.mbti` diff reviewed; every deprecation names its replacement
- [ ] Tests pin the new behaviour on all relevant targets

title: [cross-package-22] Range spellings: five conventions
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **cross-package-22**, Part 2 (smaller API finding from the `cross-package` report). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**Range spellings: five conventions** (Low · API · breaking to fix: no)

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### cross-package-22 — Range spellings: five conventions
_Low · API · breaking to fix: no · from the [`cross-package` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620751625)_

| shape | where |
|---|---|
| `start? / end?` | 34 view/slice fns (builtin) |
| `start~ / end~` required | 14 `unsafe_view`/`unsafe_substring` |
| `start_offset? / end_offset?` | `String::char_length*`, `offset_of_nth_char` (4) |
| `offset? / length?` | `Bytes::to_unchecked_string` |

body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **path-5**, Part 2 (smaller API finding from the `path` report). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### path-5 — Node naming on a pathlib-shaped type, and `resolve` means something else in Python
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: deprecate-then-remove · from the [`path` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620751109)_

- **Where:** the `path` mbti.
- **What:**
  - The type is Rust/pathlib-shaped (a value with methods and `/`), but the method names are Node's (`basename`, `dirname`, `extname`, which in Node are free functions on strings).
  - `Path::resolve` is lexical plus cwd. Python's `Path.resolve()` follows symlinks, which here is `@fs.realpath`; Rust's `std::path::absolute` and Python's `absolute()` are the lexical versions.
  - Mixed return types: `basename`/`extname` return `StringView`, while `dirname` returns `Path`.
  - `dirname("/")` returns `"/"` and `basename("/")` returns `""`, so callers can't tell "no parent" or "no file name" apart from a real value (Rust: `parent() -> Option`, `file_name() -> Option`).
- **Fix:** Before 1.0, pick one vocabulary. Suggested (Rust/pathlib):
  - `file_name() -> StringView?`
  - `parent() -> Path?`
  - `extension() -> StringView?`, without the dot (or `suffix` with the dot, as pathlib)
  - `absolute() -> Path raise ResolveError`, instead of `resolve`
  - `normalize_lexically()`

  Keep the Node names as deprecated aliases if wanted.

title: [net-compress-13] HTTP API asymmetries and label inconsistencies
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **net-compress-13**, Part 2 (smaller API finding from the `net-compress` report). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**HTTP API asymmetries and label inconsistencies** (Medium · API · breaking to fix: yes)

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### net-compress-13 — HTTP API asymmetries and label inconsistencies
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`net-compress` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620750602)_

- Where: `async/http/pkg.generated.mbti`, `request.mbt:139-176`, `client_connection.mbt:58-61`,
  `server.mbt:37`.
- What:
  - `request_text`/`request_json` take **`headers~` (required)**, while every other helper takes
    `headers?`.
  - The free functions have `post_binary/post_text/post_json/put_*/request_binary/...`, but
    `Client` only has `get_*`, `post`, `put` and `request`. There is no `Client::post_json` etc.
  - `post_json`/`request_json` never set `Content-Type: application/json` (grep: no
    `Content-Type` in non-test code).
  - `ClientConnection::connect` writes `Host`/`User-Agent` into the **caller's** `headers` map
    (`headers["Host"] = ...`). `@websocket.from_http_client` likewise mutates `extra_headers`.
    `Client::Client`'s doc says the map's ownership is transferred. A stdlib should copy instead.
  - Constructor style is mixed. `Server::Server` and `ClientConnection::ClientConnection` are
    `T(...)` with `#alias(new, deprecated)`, but `ServerConnection::new` is still `::new`. Docs
    still say `@http.ClientConnection::new` (`request.mbt:185,203,221`,
    `client_connection.js.mbt:301`).
  - `ServerConnection` has `write_string`/`write_string_interpolation`; `ClientConnection` does not.
  - Client vs server lifecycle: `end_request()` both finishes the body and reads the response, while
    `end_response()` only finishes. A client cannot do `Expect: 100-continue` (read the interim
    response before sending the body). `on_informational_response` fires only after the body is sent.
  - `Headers = Map[CaseInsensitiveString, String]` joins repeated fields with `,`. That is fine for
    reading, but there is no way to *send* repeated fields (e.g. multiple `WWW-Authenticate`/`Link`).
    Decide before 1.0 whether `Headers` stays a `Map`.
  - Parse failures leak `Failure` (see the CL finding), next to the typed `HttpProtocolError`.
- Fix: make `headers?` uniform. Mirror the free-function set on `Client`, or drop the free
  `post_*`/`put_*` variants. Set the JSON content type. Copy caller maps. Rename to
  `ServerConnection::ServerConnection` with `#alias(new, deprecated)`. Split `end_request()` into
  `finish_request()` + `read_response()` and keep the combined helper.
- Source: me (Codex raised the lifecycle point).

## Code (pinned to `0cf74cb9c`)

- [`async/http/request.mbt:139-176`](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/blob/0cf74cb9c9e8e0508024e5bd7d600648ce5c3fac/async/http/request.mbt#L139-L176)

### async-io-21 — fs completeness and labels vs Rust std::fs / Tokio
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`async-io` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620750078)_

- **Where:** `async/fs/pkg.generated.mbti`.
- **Missing:**
  - `File` has no `seek`/position and no `set_len`/truncate (codex).
  - No `copy`, `hard_link`, `read_link`, `set_times` or `chown`.
  - No `metadata()` struct: `atime`, `mtime`, `ctime`, `kind` and `file_size` each issue a separate stat. Add `stat(path, follow_symlink?) -> Metadata`.
  - `Timestamp` has no constructor or conversion to a core time type.
- **Labels and semantics:**
  - `mkdir(allow_exist?)` vs `create(allow_existing?)` vs `remove(allow_missing?)`.
  - `mkdir(p, recursive=true)` raises `File exists` on an existing dir (verified by test), unlike `mkdir -p` and `create_dir_all`. Recursive should imply allow-existing.
  - `rmdir(p, recursive=true, allow_missing=true)` raises `No such file or directory` on a missing path (verified by test): `opendir_aux` runs before the `allow_missing` catch (`dir.mbt:86` vs `:99`).
  - `tmpdir(prefix~)` *creates* a directory, though the name reads like a query. Rename to `make_temp_dir`.
  - `walk`'s callback receives names without kinds (`(String, Array[String])`, files and dirs mixed). Its default `max_concurrency=1000` can hold up to 1000 directory fds while `f` runs, which exceeds macOS's default `ulimit -n` of 256.
  - `File` exposes a public `text` field and `FsEvent`/`Mode`/`SyncMode`/`Lock`/`CreateMode` are `pub(all)` and not `#non_exhaustive`, while `FileKind` is.
- **Path type:**
  - Everything takes `StringView` and returns `String`; the new `@path.Path(String)` is used nowhere in `async/`.
  - Inconsistent within the batch: `Watcher(String)`, `redirect_to_file(String)`, `redirect_from_file(String)`, `glob(String, cwd? : String)`, shell `cwd? : String`.
  - Decide before 1.0: either fs/process accept `@path.Path` (or a `ToPath`-style trait), or document `StringView` as the path currency and make every path parameter `StringView`.

body:

### async-io-18 — TLS configuration surface is thin and has a typo
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`async-io` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620750078)_

- **Where:** `async/tls/pkg.generated.mbti`; `tls.mbt:68-71`.
- **What's wrong:**
  - **Typo:** `X509FileType::ANS1` should be `ASN1` (better: `DER`).
  - **Config is file paths only:** `Tls::server` takes only file paths (`private_key_file?`, `certificate_file?`, `pfx_file?`, all `String`), and `TrustedRoot::CustomPemFile(String)` is a path. There is no in-memory PEM/DER, no ALPN, no client certificates, no minimum version. A `TlsConfig` value (`Tls::client(inner, config~)`) would let these grow without breaking.
  - **Unclean EOF passes as clean EOF:** `openssl.mbt:527-533` returns EOF when the transport closes without `close_notify`, and Schannel does the same (`schannel.mbt:358`). That is a truncation risk for EOF-delimited messages, and there is no policy switch (codex, verified by reading).
  - **Doc errors:** `Tls::close` docs reference a non-existent `.terminate()` (it is `.shutdown()`).
  - **Leaked helpers:** `sha1` and `rand_bytes` are visible in the mbti (`#internal` but not `#doc(hidden)`) and belong in an internal package.
- **Proposed fix:** rename to `X509FileType::{Pem, Der}`; introduce `TlsConfig`; add `strict_eof? : Bool`.
- **Source:** both

title: [async-runtime-20] Naming and shape nits (grouped)
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **async-runtime-20**, Part 2 (smaller API finding from the `async-runtime` report). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**Naming and shape nits (grouped)** (Low · API · breaking to fix: deprecate-then-remove)

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### async-runtime-20 — Naming and shape nits (grouped)
_Low · API · breaking to fix: deprecate-then-remove · from the [`async-runtime` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620749451)_

- `TaskGroup::return_immediately` does not return immediately: it requests cancellation and the group still joins. A name like `cancel_remaining`/`finish` fits better. `with_timeout_opt`'s doc ("will return `None` immediately") likewise ignores shielded cleanup. *(codex + me)*
- `Cond` is a notify primitive without an associated lock, and drops a signal when nobody waits (documented). Consider `Notify`/`Event` naming, which also avoids the `cond_var` vs `Cond` mismatch. *(codex)*
- `@aqueue.Kind::{DiscardOldest, DiscardLatest}`: the antonyms do not pair. Use `DiscardOldest`/`DiscardNewest`.
- Error names mix three conventions: `TimeoutError`/`OsError`/`JsError`, `TimerCancelled`/`QueueAlreadyClosed`/`WaitedTaskAlreadyCancelled`, and `BreakFromSpawnLoop`/`KilledBySignal`.
- Missing observers and helpers that Tokio, Trio and Go all have:
  - `Queue::length`, `Queue::is_closed`
  - `Semaphore::available` (`size` is public, the count is not)
  - `Lazy::peek` (`@lazy.Lazy` has `peek`)
  - `Task::is_done`
  - `Mutex::with_lock[X](f)` / `Semaphore::with_permit[X](f)`, so callers stop writing `acquire(); defer release()` by hand
- `any([])` raises `Failure("no tasks provided")` (`async.mbt:327`). That is a precondition violation: either `abort`, or raise a typed error.
- `set_global_cancellation_signals` is silently reset after every `with_event_loop` (`event_loop/signal.mbt`, `global_signal_handler_initialized.val = false`), so a setting made before the first loop does not survive a second loop.

body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **async-runtime-10**, Part 2 (smaller API finding from the `async-runtime` report). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**Platform-dependent `Fd` type, and generated interfaces that show only one target** (Medium · API · breaking to fix: yes)

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### async-runtime-10 — Platform-dependent `Fd` type, and generated interfaces that show only one target
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`async-runtime` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620749451)_

- Where: `async/types/types.mbt:18,25,45`. `Fd` is `UInt64` on wasm, an opaque `#external` type on Windows, and `Int32` on native Unix. Every public `fd()` getter returns it (`PipeRead::fd`, `Tcp::fd`, `File::fd`, `Input::fd`, ...). Because it is an alias, the mbti expands it to `UInt64`, which is wrong on native Unix.
- What:
  - Portable code cannot do anything with an fd, not even print it: Windows has no `Show` and no `to_int`.
  - The published interface (`pkg.generated.mbti`, mooncakes docs) is evidently generated for the wasm target. It shows `Fd = UInt64` and omits native-only API: `@async.set_external_event_loop` (`integration.mbt:28`, `#cfg(target="native")`) is absent from `async/pkg.generated.mbti`.
  - Signatures also differ by backend without any trace in the interface. On wasm-gc, `@event_loop.sleep` is `async fn sleep(Int32) -> Unit` (raising; `unimplemented.mbt`) while native/js have `noraise`, and `@async` re-exports it.
- Fix: make `Fd` an opaque newtype on every platform, with explicit `Fd::to_int64()` (or a `RawFd` per platform) plus `Eq`/`Hash`/`Debug`. Document per-target availability in the README, or generate per-target mbti sections. Make the wasm-gc stubs' signatures match.
- Source: me

body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **mutable-collections-16**, Part 2 (smaller API finding from the `mutable-collections` report). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

### mutable-collections-16 — Naming and convention nits (grouped)
_Low · API · breaking to fix: deprecate-then-remove · from the [`mutable-collections` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620747729)_

- **`LazyList::empty()`** is still the live `#as_free_fn` primary constructor, while `List` deprecated `new`/`empty` for `List([])` (#4289), and `LazyList(xs)` now exists (`d048e308f`). Either deprecate `empty` in favour of `LazyList([])`, or un-deprecate `List`'s.
- **LazyList is missing basics**: `length`, `Eq`, `nth`/`get`, `find`, `any`/`all`, `unfold`/`iterate`/`repeat` (the common infinite-list builders), and a strict `cons`. `zip` lacks the `#as_free_fn` that `List::zip` has. `LazyList::iter` allocates a closure per element (`advance = () => tail.force()`); store the current cell instead.
- **`List::unsafe_tail`** is still public and visible in the mbti, while `unsafe_head`, `unsafe_last` and `unsafe_nth` are `#internal(unsafe)` + `#doc(hidden)`. Hide it the same way, and give the plain name `tail` to an `Option`-returning version once the deprecated `tail` is gone.
- **`List::add`**: the alias on `prepend` is now deprecated. Once it is removed, promote `Add::add` per AGENTS.md (List impls `Add` but has no promoted `add`).
- **Deprecation messages for `ToJson::to_json` disagree.** `hashmap`, `hashset`, `set`, `sorted_map`, `deque` and `priority_queue` say "Use `@json.to_json` instead"; `sorted_set`, `queue` and `list` say "Use `Json(value)` instead". AGENTS.md says `Json(x)`.
- **`array/moon.pkg`** lists target rules for files that don't exist (`array_js.mbt`, `array_nonjs.mbt`, `blit_js.mbt`, `blit_nonjs.mbt`). `array/README.mbt.md:3` still advertises the deprecated `View` alias.
- **`set/linked_hash_set.mbt:142`** has a stale `FIXME:(upstream)` comment about `ArrayView::each`.
- **The `Deque` invariants doc contradicts itself** (`deque/types.mbt`): "If the buffer is empty: `head == 0`" vs "When `len == 0`: `head` is zero or a valid buffer index". `extract_if` can leave `len == 0` with `head != 0`.
- **`HashSet::iter` doesn't state that its order is unspecified** (HashMap's does).

body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **mutable-collections-12**, Part 2 (smaller API finding from the `mutable-collections` report). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### mutable-collections-12 — Deque's signatures still disagree with Array's (open #4272 item, unchanged)
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: deprecate-then-remove · from the [`mutable-collections` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620747729)_

- **Where**:
  - `Deque::drain(start~ : Int, len? : Int)` vs `Array::drain(Int, Int)` (start and **end**, positional).
  - `Deque::blit_to(.., len~ : Int, ..)` (required) vs `Array::blit_to(.., len? : Int, ..)`.
  - `Deque::append(Self, Self)` vs `Array::append(Self, ArrayView[T])`.
  - `Deque::chunks -> Self[Self[A]]` vs `Array::chunks -> Self[ArrayView[T]]`.
  - `Deque::join(Self[String], StringView)` vs `Array::join[A : ToStringView]`.
  - Deque also has no `fold`, `rev_fold`, `foldi`, `any` or `all`; Array has them all, and so does Queue (`fold`).
- **What**: Of these, `drain` is the dangerous one: the same-looking call means `[start, end)` on Array but `(start, length)` on Deque.
- **Fix**: As in #4272: one `drain` convention, `len?` on `blit_to`, `append(ArrayView[A])`, `join[A : ToStringView]`, and add `fold`/`rev_fold`.
- **Also**: `Deque::chunks` allocates `capacity=size` for every chunk (`deque/deque.mbt:1913`). `Deque([x]).chunks(1_000_000_000)` allocates a billion slots. Use `min(size, len - i)`. (Codex finding; confirmed from reading.)

### mutable-collections-11 — Queue keeps references to removed elements and offers no way to release them
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: no · from the [`mutable-collections` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620747729)_

### mutable-collections-10 — SortedMap still lacks most of the Map/HashMap mutation API; its `get_or_init`/`update_or_default` contract is stricter than its siblings'
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: no · from the [`mutable-collections` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620747729)_

### numerics-15 — Floating-point nits
_Low · Docs/API · breaking to fix: no · from the [`numerics` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620747252)_

- `double/README.mbt.md:24` and `float/README.mbt.md:24` say "An explicit, opt-in total comparator … is deferred". `Double::total_compare` and `Float::total_compare` shipped in cdfa6c351, so the README is stale.
- The name `total_compare` suggests IEEE totalOrder (Rust's `total_cmp`), but the implementation puts NaN first and treats signed zeros as equal (`builtin/double_total_compare.mbt:14-27`). Either rename it (for example `nan_first_compare`) or say so in the first line of the doc.
- `@double.not_a_number` is `0x7FF8000000000001` (`double/limits.mbt:17`), a non-canonical payload. `@float.not_a_number` is the canonical `0x7FC00000`, and `0.0/0.0` is `0x7FF8000000000000` (verified on all backends).
- `Show` and `@debug.repr` both print `-0.0` as `0`, so Debug loses the sign.
- `@math` results are within 2 ulp of Apple libm on every backend. I checked 4 000 samples for each of 22 double and 20 float functions; maxima were 2 ulp for tan, tanh, asinh, acosh, atanh, tanf and tanhf, and 1 ulp elsewhere, so there are no gross port errors. Results are not bit-identical across backends, though: js uses the host `Math.*`, and native and wasm-gc already differ on 3% of `sin`/`cos` samples. Document this.
- Missing from `@math`: `log10f`/`log2f` (#4272), `exp2`, `copysign`, `fma`, `fmod`/`remainder`, `frexp`/`ldexp`, `nextafter`, `erf`, `gamma`, and the constants `E`, `TAU`, `LN2` and `EPSILON`.

title: [numerics-11] BigInt signatures to settle (beyond #4272's `abs`/`signum`/`to_octets` items)
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **numerics-11**, Part 2 (smaller API finding from the `numerics` report). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**BigInt signatures to settle (beyond #4272's `abs`/`signum`/`to_octets` items)** (Medium · API · breaking to fix: yes)

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### numerics-11 — BigInt signatures to settle (beyond #4272's `abs`/`signum`/`to_octets` items)
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`numerics` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620747252)_

- **Where:** `bigint/pkg.generated.mbti`.
- **What:**
  - `pub fn BigInt::pow(Self, Self, modulus? : Self) -> Self` takes the exponent as a `BigInt`, so callers write `2N.pow(100N)`. Without a modulus, any exponent beyond Int range is infeasible anyway.
  - With `modulus`, the result is the non-negative residue: `(-3N).pow(3N, modulus=5N)` = 3. `%` truncates instead: `-27N % 5N` = -2. Neither difference is documented.
  - `to_octets(length?)` treats `length` as a *minimum*: `256N.to_octets(length=1)` returns 2 bytes (verified).
  - `from_octets(BytesView, signum? : Int)` takes a sign as an `Int`.
  - `ctz(0N)` = 0, while `Int::ctz(0)` = 32 and Java's `getLowestSetBit(0)` = -1.
  - `bit_length` uses two's-complement semantics (`(-1N).bit_length()` = 0, `(-2N)` = 1, matching Java but not Python).
  - Missing: `div_rem`, floor division, `gcd`, `isqrt`, `test_bit`, `abs`, `signum`, and `to_double`/`from_double`.
- **Fix:**
  - `pow(Self, Int) -> Self` plus `pow_mod(Self, exp : Self, modulus : Self) -> Self` (documented to return a value in [0, m)).
  - `to_be_bytes(min_length? : Int)` / `from_be_bytes(BytesView, negative? : Bool)`, or a two's-complement pair.
  - Define and document `ctz(0)`.
- **Source:** me. Codex contributed the `length` label.

_Medium · API · breaking to fix: partly · from the [`numerics` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620747252)_

title: [text-15] Encoding-family gaps and one odd lossy rule
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **text-15**, Part 2 (smaller API finding from the `text` report). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**Encoding-family gaps and one odd lossy rule** (Low · API · breaking to fix: no)

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### text-15 — Encoding-family gaps and one odd lossy rule
_Low · API · breaking to fix: no · from the [`text` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620746724)_

- `hex` has no `decode_lossy`, while every sibling does (`encoding/hex/pkg.generated.mbti`).
- `base64.decode_lossy` *skips* invalid characters but *stops* at whitespace unless `ignore_whitespace=true` (`encoding/base64/decode.mbt:163-178`), so `"SGVs bG8="` decodes to `Hel` and `"SGVs!bG8="` to `Hello`. Whitespace should be the most forgivable character, not the least.
- `base64` has no URL-safe alphabet (RFC 4648 §5, needed for JWT). An `alphabet?`/`url_safe?` label could be added later without breaking anything.
- `percent` is text→text only (`encode(StringView) -> String`). RFC 3986 escapes octets, so binary or non-UTF-8 payloads cannot be encoded, and `decode` raises on non-UTF-8 escapes. Add `encode_bytes(BytesView)` / `decode_bytes(StringView) -> Bytes`.
- Every encoder returns a fresh `Bytes`/`String`. There is no variant that appends into a `Buffer`/`StringBuilder`, so `@base64.encode` inside a larger document costs an extra copy. Additive.
- **Source:** me.

title: [P1-39] random/env: Rand::int(limit=0), per-target @env.args(), wasm-gc fixed seed, stream stability
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-39**, Part 1 (Tooling / prelude). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**`Rand::int(limit=0)` means full range**; `@env.args()` shape differs per target; `Rand()` fixed seed on wasm-gc; stream stability unpromised (it is ChaCha8Rand — document it). [tooling:70,76,88]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### tooling-9 — `Rand::int/uint/int64/uint64(limit=0)` means "full range", so an empty-collection draw silently returns a huge value
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`tooling` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620748867)_

- **Where**: `random/random.mbt` `Rand::int(self, limit~ : Int32 = 0)`, `if limit == 0 { (self.next() >> 33).to_int() }`, and the same pattern in `uint`/`int64`/`uint64`. splitmix `next_uint64(limit? : UInt64)` aborts on `Some(0)` (`splitmix/random.mbt:71`).
- **Evidence**: verified by test. `let n = 0; r.int(limit=n)` returned `1538906883`. In `xs[r.int(limit=xs.length())]` that becomes a confusing out-of-bounds error far from the cause, where it should abort at the draw.
- **Fix**: Change the parameter to `limit? : Int32` with `None` meaning the full range, and abort on an explicit `0`, as splitmix does. This sharpens the open #4272 High item (random vs splitmix semantics). While here, add the missing bounded-range form, `Rand::int(self, min? : Int, max? : Int)` (half-open, matching `double(min~, max~)`), plus `Rand::shuffle_array[T](Self, MutArrayView[T])` and `Rand::choice[T](Self, ArrayView[T]) -> T?`.
- Source: me (codex #11 agrees)

### tooling-10 — Stream stability is never promised for `random`, and `Rand()` silently uses a fixed seed on wasm-gc
_Medium · Docs/API · breaking to fix: no · from the [`tooling` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620748867)_

- **Where**: `random/random.mbt:58-66`, `Rand::Rand(generator?)`: `match @env.rand(32) { Some(seed) => chacha8(seed~); None => Rand::chacha8() }`. `env/env_wasm.mbt` makes `rand_internal` always return `false` on wasm-gc.
- **What's wrong**:
  1. On wasm-gc every `Rand()` produces the same stream, seeded with `"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ123456"`, and callers have no way to detect it. The README mentions this, but the API does not expose it.
  2. Nothing documents whether `Rand::chacha8(seed)` streams are stable across releases and backends. The implementation is in fact bit-compatible with Go's `ChaCha8Rand` (C2SP chacha8rand): the first output for the default seed is `13219109469176600229` = `0xb773b6063d4616a5`, which is Go's test vector. That is a guarantee worth stating. The mapping from the stream to `int`/`uint`/`double`/`shuffle`, such as `int()` = `next >> 33` and `uint()` = the low 32 bits, should be explicitly stable or explicitly unstable.
  3. Nothing says the generator is not a CSPRNG: there is no reseeding and there is the fixed fallback seed.
- **Fix**:
  - Document "`Rand::chacha8(seed).uint64()` yields the C2SP chacha8rand stream; it is stable across versions and targets", and state whether the derived methods are stable.
  - Add `Rand::from_entropy() -> Rand?`, or have `Rand()` mix `@env.now()` into the fallback.
  - Take `seed : BytesView` (`ChaCha8` already does).
- Source: both (fallback: codex #9; stream compatibility: me)

### tooling-11 — `@env.args()` has a different shape on each target
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`tooling` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620748867)_

- **Where**: `env/env.mbt:17-19` doc. JS returns `process.argv`, which includes the node executable and the script path. Other targets return `[program, ...]`. `argparse/parser.mbt:81-97` has to carry two `#cfg` copies of `default_argv` to strip one or two leading entries.
- **What's wrong**: Every portable CLI has to repeat argparse's `#cfg` split. After 1.0 the JS shape is frozen.
- **Fix**: Normalise `args()` to `[program, ...user_args]` on every target, or add `pub fn user_args() -> ArrayView[String]` (with the program name already stripped) and point users at it. argparse's `default_argv` then collapses to one line.
- Source: me

_Medium · API · breaking to fix: deprecate-then-remove · from the [`builtin` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620746235)_

body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-37**, Part 1 (Tooling / prelude). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

### tooling-3 — `Debug` is `pub(open)`, but every `Repr` builder is `#doc(hidden)`
_High · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`tooling` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620748867)_

- **Where**: `debug/pkg.generated.mbti` exposes only `Repr::Repr[T : Debug](T)`, `Repr::to_string`, `render`, and `pub(open) trait Debug { fn to_repr(Self) -> Repr }`. `debug/repr.mbt:152-299` holds `#doc(hidden) pub fn Repr::{traverse, integer, double, float, bool, char, string, tuple, array, record, opaque_, literal, map, omitted, unit, ctor}`.
- **What's wrong**: A user who has to write `impl Debug` by hand cannot build a `Repr` with the documented API. This is the case for abstract types, types holding closures, and types that want an opaque `<Name: ...>` form. They can only delegate to another type's `Repr(x)`. Inside core, bench, random, argparse, quickcheck (`observation.mbt:44` `Repr::record`), json, v128, bytes/string regex, sorted_map/set, vector(_map), priority_queue, socket, os_error and others all call the hidden builders. The README only covers `derive(Debug)`.
- **Fix**: Pick the supported subset now, rename it, and unhide it. Suggested set: `Repr::constructor(name, args : ArrayView[(String?, Repr)])`, `Repr::record(fields)`, `Repr::opaque(name, contents? : Repr)` (replacing `opaque_`), `Repr::literal(text)`, `Repr::array`/`tuple`/`map`, and `Repr::omitted()`. Keep `traverse` and the scalar leaf builders hidden, or deprecate them. Document a hand-written impl in `debug/README.mbt.md`.

body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-36**, Part 1 (async API shape). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**Exhaustive public enums + `os_error` exposes runtime helpers; `runtime_internal` is a public non-experimental package**; sync primitives split across three single-type packages. [async-runtime:124,133,154]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### async-runtime-15 — Sync-primitive layout: three single-type packages re-exported partially from root, `Mutex` in root
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: deprecate-then-remove · from the [`async-runtime` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620749451)_

- Where: `async/async.mbt` `pub using @aqueue {type Queue}`, `@semaphore {type Semaphore}`, `@cond_var {type Cond}`. `Mutex`, `Lazy` and `Timer` are defined in root.
- What:
  - Each type has two import paths.
  - The re-export is partial. `@aqueue.Kind` and `@aqueue.QueueAlreadyClosed` are not re-exported, so catching a closed queue still needs `@aqueue`.
  - No package needs these packages independently of `@async`. The only other importers (`async/websocket`, `async/tls`) import `@async` too, and use `@semaphore.Semaphore` as a lock instead of `@async.Mutex`.
- Fix: pick one home before 1.0. Either fold `aqueue`/`semaphore`/`cond_var` into root (or into `async/sync`) and deprecate the single-type packages, or move `Mutex` next to `Semaphore` and re-export everything, including `Kind` and the error types.

- `@types.Platform` (`types.mbt:50`, `pub(all)`, no `#non_exhaustive`, no `Eq`/`Debug`). Adding FreeBSD or Android later breaks every exhaustive `match platform`.
- `@signal.Signal` (`signal.mbt`, `pub(all)`, SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGBREAK). Adding SIGQUIT or SIGUSR1 is breaking. Mark both `#non_exhaustive` now.
- `@os_error.Kind` is `#non_exhaustive`, but `Unknown` is a public constructor (TODO at `error_kind.mbt`). Code matching `Unknown` silently changes meaning whenever a kind is added. Only 6 kinds exist; Rust's `io::ErrorKind` has ~40. Missing kinds will be hit at once: `IsADirectory`, `DirectoryNotEmpty`, `BrokenPipe`, `ConnectionReset`, `AddrInUse`, `TimedOut`, `Interrupted`, `InvalidInput`.

title: [P1-35] async: process exit status is an overloaded Int32; accept reports wildcard local address
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-35**, Part 1 (async API shape). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**Process exit status is an overloaded `Int32`** (signals as `-signal_number`, `async/process/process.mbt:179`); TCP `accept` reports the listener's wildcard address as the local address (`async/socket/tcp.mbt:199`). [async-io:197,247]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### async-io-17 — TCP/UDP surface: ambiguous `addr`, wrong local address on accept, split UDP types, C-style names
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`async-io` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620750078)_

- **Where:** `async/socket/tcp.mbt:17-24` and `:310-314`, `:195`, `:222`; `udp.mbt:48`.
- **What's wrong:**
  - `Tcp` has both a public field `addr` and a method `addr()`, and the field means the *local* address (the peer address only comes from `accept`'s tuple).
  - Accepted connections set `addr: self.addr` (`tcp.mbt:195`, `:222`). On a wildcard listener that is `0.0.0.0` or `::`, not the real local address. The comment at `:195` asserts the wrong invariant. (codex, verified by reading)
  - `UdpClient` and `UdpServer` duplicate four multicast setters, and you cannot "bind locally, then connect" (codex). `recvfrom`/`sendto` are C spellings next to `send`/`recv`. `send(Bytes, offset?, len?)` contrasts with `write(BytesView)`.
  - `UdpClient` registers with `read_only=true` (`udp.mbt:48`), so if a `send` hits EAGAIN, `wait_write` waits on an event that is never registered (codex, plausible from reading, not tested).
  - Missing: `peer_addr`, `set_nodelay` (always on, `tcp.mbt:191`), half-close (see the flush/shutdown finding), Unix-domain sockets.
- **Proposed fix:**
  - Make fields `priv`; add `Tcp::local_addr()` and `Tcp::peer_addr()`; call `getsockname` on accepted sockets.
  - Use one `UdpSocket::bind(addr)` + `connect(addr)`, with `send(BytesView)`, `send_to(BytesView, Addr)` and `recv_from`.
- **Source:** both

### async-io-20 — Process exit status is an overloaded `Int32`, plus redundant variants
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`async-io` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620750078)_

- **Where:** `process.mbt:178-190` ("If killed by a signal, the result would be `-signal_number`"), `ProcessResult.exit_code : Int32`, `wait_pid(Int32) -> Int32` (public).
- **Evidence (verified by test):** `run("sh", ["-c", "kill -9 $$"]).exit_code == -9`.
- **What's wrong:**
  - On Windows, exit codes are 32-bit and NTSTATUS values are negative as `Int32` (for example `0xC0000005`), so the encoding is ambiguous there.
  - There is no `kill(signal)` on `Process` (only `cancel()` via the handler).
  - `ProcessInput::{Inherit, Stdin}` and `ProcessOutput::{Inherit, Stdout}` overlap.
  - `FromFile(StringView)`, `ToFile(StringView)` and `AppendFile(StringView)` store views in a public enum, while `redirect_to_file(String)` takes `String`.
- **Proposed fix:**
  - `enum ExitStatus { Exited(Int32), Signaled(@signal.Signal) }` with `success()`.
  - `Process::kill(signal? : @signal.Signal)`.
  - Drop or alias the duplicate variants.
  - Store `String` in enum payloads.
- **Source:** me

title: [P1-34] tls: transport close without close_notify is reported as clean EOF
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-34**, Part 1 (async API shape). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**TLS truncation policy**: a transport close without TLS `close_notify` is reported as clean EOF (`async/tls/openssl.mbt:527`, deliberate) — EOF-delimited protocols can't detect truncation. Expose a strict mode / distinguishable error. (new, from Codex; verified by reading)

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### async-io-18 — TLS configuration surface is thin and has a typo
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`async-io` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620750078)_

- **Where:** `async/tls/pkg.generated.mbti`; `tls.mbt:68-71`.
- **What's wrong:**
  - **Typo:** `X509FileType::ANS1` should be `ASN1` (better: `DER`).
  - **Config is file paths only:** `Tls::server` takes only file paths (`private_key_file?`, `certificate_file?`, `pfx_file?`, all `String`), and `TrustedRoot::CustomPemFile(String)` is a path. There is no in-memory PEM/DER, no ALPN, no client certificates, no minimum version. A `TlsConfig` value (`Tls::client(inner, config~)`) would let these grow without breaking.
  - **Unclean EOF passes as clean EOF:** `openssl.mbt:527-533` returns EOF when the transport closes without `close_notify`, and Schannel does the same (`schannel.mbt:358`). That is a truncation risk for EOF-delimited messages, and there is no policy switch (codex, verified by reading).
  - **Doc errors:** `Tls::close` docs reference a non-existent `.terminate()` (it is `.shutdown()`).
  - **Leaked helpers:** `sha1` and `rand_bytes` are visible in the mbti (`#internal` but not `#doc(hidden)`) and belong in an internal package.
- **Proposed fix:** rename to `X509FileType::{Pem, Der}`; introduce `TlsConfig`; add `strict_eof? : Bool`.

title: [P1-33] socket: Addr truncates ports, ip() is 0 for IPv6, ordering compares port first
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-33**, Part 1 (async API shape). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**`@socket.Addr`**: port silently truncated (70000 → 4464), `ip()` returns 0 for IPv6, ordering compares port before IP. [async-io:180]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### async-io-16 — `@socket.Addr` is IPv4-shaped, lossy, and orders by raw sockaddr bytes
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`async-io` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620750078)_

- **Where:**
  - `async/socket/addr.mbt:22` (`#derive(Eq, Compare, Hash) struct Addr(Bytes)`, a raw sockaddr).
  - `Addr::new(UInt32, Int32)` at `:62`.
  - `Addr::ip() -> UInt32`, `Addr::port() -> Int32`.
- **Evidence (verified by test):**
  - `Addr::new(0x7f000001, 70000)` gives `127.0.0.1:4464`, and port `-1` gives `65535` (silent truncation).
  - `Addr::parse("[2001:db8::1]:80").ip()` returns `0`.
  - `Addr::parse("10.0.0.1:80") < Addr::parse("9.0.0.1:81")` is `true`: the order compares the port before the IP and depends on the platform's sockaddr layout (BSD `sin_len`).
  - There is no public IPv6 constructor, IPv6 bytes accessor or scope-id accessor.
- **Proposed fix:**
  - `Addr::new(ip : IpAddr, port : UInt16)` with `enum IpAddr { V4(UInt32), V6(Bytes /*16*/, scope_id~ : UInt32) }`.
  - `Addr::ip() -> IpAddr` and `Addr::port() -> UInt16`.
  - Implement `Compare` by family, then IP, then port (or drop `Compare`).
  - Make `Addr::resolve` take `StringView`, like `Tcp::connect_to_host`.
- **Source:** both (IPv6 accessor: codex; truncation and ordering: me)

title: [P1-32] async io: Reader/Writer lack flush/shutdown; three pipe() functions
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-32**, Part 1 (async API shape). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**Reader/Writer**: no `flush`/`shutdown`, no TCP half-close; three `pipe()` functions and two `PipeRead`/`PipeWrite` pairs; platform-varying fd alias leaks; `raw_fd` mbti stale. [async-io:116,150,161,170]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### async-io-10 — Writer trait has no `flush` or `shutdown`; TCP has no half-close
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: deprecate-then-remove · from the [`async-io` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620750078)_

- **Where:** `async/io/binary_writer.mbt:43-46` (`BinaryWriter { write, write_reader }`); `BufferedWriter::flush` is inherent only (`buffered_writer.mbt:54`); `Tls::shutdown` is Tls-only; `Tcp` exposes only `close` (`socket/tcp.mbt:27`).
- **What's wrong:**
  - Wrap a `BufferedWriter` as `&BinaryWriter` (for example, under `Utf8Writer` or as the TLS transport, `tls/transport.mbt:74`) and its buffer can no longer be flushed.
  - Generic code cannot signal EOF to a peer.
  - Without TCP half-close, an EOF-delimited request (send, then read the response until EOF) cannot be written.
  - Tokio's `AsyncWrite` has `poll_flush` and `poll_shutdown`.
- **Proposed fix:** add `async fn flush(Self) -> Unit = _` (default no-op) and `async fn shutdown(Self) -> Unit = _` (default flush), implemented by BufferedWriter, Tls, Tcp (`shutdown(SHUT_WR)`), the pipes and WriteToProcess. Adding defaulted methods is not breaking, but the contract ("`write` does not imply flush") must be fixed in the docs before 1.0.
- **Related:**
  - `BufferedWriter` does not bypass the buffer for writes larger than capacity (an extra copy).
  - If an inner write fails partway, a later `flush` re-sends the already-committed prefix (`buffered_writer.mbt:57`; codex, verified by reading).
- **Source:** both

### async-io-13 — Reader/Writer naming and EOF semantics
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`async-io` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620750078)_

- **Where:** `async/io/pkg.generated.mbti` (traits) and `raw_fd` (`RawFd::read`/`write`).
- **What's wrong:**
  - `read()` returns a chunk as `Bytes?`, and `read_into(buf)` is what Rust/Tokio call `read`. That is acceptable, but then `RawFd::read(buf)` means "single syscall into buf", the opposite of `@io`'s `read`. `RawFd::write` returns a count while `BinaryWriter::write` writes everything (codex point 4). Pick one meaning: rename RawFd's to `read_into` / `write_once` (or `write_some`), or adopt Tokio's `write` vs `write_all` pair.
  - `ReaderClosed` is raised for an unexpected EOF, not for using a closed reader. The name is misleading, and the closed-reader case has no error at all (it aborts or segfaults, see above). There are also three EOF-ish errors: `@io.ReaderClosed`, `@io.PipeClosed`, `@tls.ConnectionClosed`. Proposal: rename to `UnexpectedEof`, and add one `Closed` error for "operation on a closed handle".
  - `read_into(.., max_len=0)` raises an untyped `Failure` (`binary_reader.mbt:115`), and so does `read_into(buf, offset=buf.length())`. Either allow 0 (and return 0) or raise a typed `InvalidArgument`.
  - `BinaryReaderImpl`/`BinaryWriterImpl`, `BinaryReaderController` and `BinaryWriterController` must be public for implementers. In return, every concrete type repeats a 12-name `pub extend` block (about 12 copies across these packages). That is acceptable under AGENTS.md, but it means any later addition to `BinaryReader` must be mirrored in about 12 extend blocks. Decide the final method list now.
  - `ensure_buffered` (in `BinaryReaderImpl`, documented "should not be invoked by users") is the only way to detect early EOF without catching `ReaderClosed`. Expose a user-facing `try_peek_exactly(n) -> BytesView?` or similar.
  - `TextReader` has no `read_line` (`\n` or `\r\n`), and `TextWriter` bakes `write_json` into the base trait while lacking `write_line`.
- **Source:** both (RawFd naming overlap: codex; the rest: me)

### async-io-14 — Three `pipe()` functions and two `PipeRead`/`PipeWrite` type pairs
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`async-io` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620750078)_

- **Where:**
  - `@io.pipe() -> (@io.PipeRead, @io.PipeWrite)`: in-memory, rendezvous, non-raising.
  - `@pipe.pipe() -> (@pipe.PipeRead, @pipe.PipeWrite) raise`: OS pipe, needs a running loop.
  - `@process.pipe() -> (SharedProcessInput, SharedProcessOutput) raise`: an OS pipe between children.
- **What's wrong:** the same names carry different semantics (buffering, raise-ness, fd availability). With both packages imported, `@io.PipeRead` and `@pipe.PipeRead` are easy to mix up in signatures.
- **Proposed fix:** rename the in-memory one to `@io.memory_pipe() -> (MemoryPipeRead, MemoryPipeWrite)`, or move it beside `MemoryReader`. Name `@process.pipe` after what it does, for example `@process.pipe_between()`.
- **Source:** me

### async-io-15 — File-descriptor type leaks an internal, platform-varying alias; `raw_fd` interface is stale
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`async-io` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620750078)_

- **Where:**
  - `File::fd`, `PipeRead::fd`, `Tcp::fd`, `TcpServer::fd`, `Udp*::fd` return `@fd_util.Fd` (an internal package). It is `Int32` on native Unix, `UInt64` on wasm and opaque on Windows (`async/types/types.mbt:14-45`). Checked-in mbtis show `UInt64` (the wasm view).
  - `@stdio.Input::fd() -> Fd raise` vs `@fs.File::fd() -> Fd`: inconsistent raise-ness.
  - `async/raw_fd/pkg.generated.mbti` is stale. It says `package "moonbitlang/async/raw_fd"` and imports `moonbitlang/async/io`, while the freshly generated `_build/native/.../raw_fd.mbti` says `moonbitlang/core/async/raw_fd`. It is not regenerated because the package is native-only.
  - `RawFd`/`RawFdStream` are `pub struct` with a public `fd` field, an async constructor, and `#alias(new, deprecated)`.
- **What's wrong:** `let n : Int = file.fd()` compiles on Linux and fails on Windows/wasm. Users cannot name the type except through `@types.Fd`.
- **Proposed fix:** make `Fd` a single opaque public type in `async/types` (or `raw_fd`) with `to_int64()` / `from_raw()` accessors. Make RawFd fields `priv` with a `fd()` method. Have CI regenerate native-only mbtis.
- **Source:** me

- [`async/io/binary_writer.mbt:43-46`](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/blob/0cf74cb9c9e8e0508024e5bd7d600648ce5c3fac/async/io/binary_writer.mbt#L43-L46)

title: [P1-31] async/process: stdio fields and ProcessResult getters abort when not redirected
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-31**, Part 1 (async API shape). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**Process stdio fields and `ProcessResult` getters are placeholders that abort** when not redirected; `DuplicateStdout` hits bare `panic()`. [async-io:84]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### async-io-7 — Process stdio fields and result getters are placeholders that abort when used
_High · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`async-io` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620750078)_

- **Where:**
  - `async/process/pkg.generated.mbti`: `Process { stdin : WriteToProcess, stdout : ReadFromProcess, stderr : ReadFromProcess }`, and `OrphanProcess` likewise.
  - `redirect.mbt:66` and `:144`: `abort("cannot read output of a process whose stdout/stderr is not redirected with Collect")`.
  - `process.mbt:31`: `ProcessResult::stdout_binary` aborts unless `Collect`.
  - `redirect.mbt:346`: `DuplicateStdout => panic()` when passed as `stdout`.
- **What's wrong:** availability depends on a runtime argument but the type says the value is always present. A typo like `stdout=Inherit` plus `p.stdout.read_all()` kills the program. `ProcessOutput` accepts `DuplicateStdout` for `stdout` even though only `stderr` can use it.
- **Evidence:** `@process.run("true", [], stdout=DuplicateStdout)` gave a bare `PanicError` and SIGABRT (verified by test).
- **Proposed fix:**
  - Make the fields `stdin : WriteToProcess?`, `stdout : ReadFromProcess?`, `stderr : ReadFromProcess?`.
  - Make the getters `ProcessResult::stdout_binary(self) -> Bytes?` (same for `stderr_binary` and `*_text`), or raise a typed error.
  - Either split `ProcessOutput` for stderr (`StderrOutput` with `DuplicateStdout`) or raise `InvalidRedirect` instead of `panic()`.
- **Source:** both

title: [P1-30] parse_int and parse_bigint accept different grammars; add a strict mode for wire formats
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-30**, Part 1 (Numerics). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**Parser grammars differ**: `+5`, `0x10`, `1_000` parse with `parse_int` but not `parse_bigint`. (HTTP's use of literal syntax is P0-2 — numeric parsing for wire formats needs a strict mode.) [numerics:131]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### numerics-7 — The integer parsers accept different grammars, and the BigInt parser is the odd one out
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: no · from the [`numerics` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620747252)_

- **Where:**
  - `bigint/bigint_wide.mbt:868` (`from_string_dec`) and `:900` (`parse_bigint`, `#internal`, re-exported as `@string.parse_bigint`).
  - `bigint/bigint_js.mbt:27,93`.
  - The `@string.parse_int` family.
- **Evidence (verified by test):**
  - `parse_int("+5")` returns `Ok(5)`, but `parse_bigint("+5")` and `parse_uint64("+5")` both fail with `Failure(invalid syntax)`.
  - `parse_int("0x10")` = 16 and `parse_int("0b11")` = 3, so the default base auto-detects prefixes. Explicit `base=10` rejects `"0x10"`. `parse_bigint("0x10")` fails.
  - `parse_int("1_000")` = 1000, but `parse_bigint("1_000")` fails.
  - `BigInt::from_string("+5")` and `("")` abort.
  - Every failure is an untyped `Failure("invalid syntax")`.
  - Formatting uses `radix~` and parsing uses `base~` (still open from #4272).
- **Fix:**
  - One grammar for every integer parser, BigInt included: optional sign, the same prefix rules, the same `_` rule.
  - One label (`radix~`).
  - A typed `ParseIntError` (empty, invalid digit, overflow).
  - Deprecate `BigInt::from_string` in favour of `@string.parse_bigint`, or make it `(StringView, radix?) -> BigInt raise`.
- **Source:** me.

title: [P1-29] bigint: to_octets(length?) treats length as a minimum
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-29**, Part 1 (Numerics). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**`BigInt::to_octets(length?)` treats `length` as a minimum** (`bigint/bigint_wide.mbt:966`) — rename `min_length` or add exact-width checked serialisation. (new, from Codex; verified by reading)

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### numerics-11 — BigInt signatures to settle (beyond #4272's `abs`/`signum`/`to_octets` items)
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`numerics` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620747252)_

- **Where:** `bigint/pkg.generated.mbti`.
- **What:**
  - `pub fn BigInt::pow(Self, Self, modulus? : Self) -> Self` takes the exponent as a `BigInt`, so callers write `2N.pow(100N)`. Without a modulus, any exponent beyond Int range is infeasible anyway.
  - With `modulus`, the result is the non-negative residue: `(-3N).pow(3N, modulus=5N)` = 3. `%` truncates instead: `-27N % 5N` = -2. Neither difference is documented.
  - `to_octets(length?)` treats `length` as a *minimum*: `256N.to_octets(length=1)` returns 2 bytes (verified).
  - `from_octets(BytesView, signum? : Int)` takes a sign as an `Int`.
  - `ctz(0N)` = 0, while `Int::ctz(0)` = 32 and Java's `getLowestSetBit(0)` = -1.
  - `bit_length` uses two's-complement semantics (`(-1N).bit_length()` = 0, `(-2N)` = 1, matching Java but not Python).
  - Missing: `div_rem`, floor division, `gcd`, `isqrt`, `test_bit`, `abs`, `signum`, and `to_double`/`from_double`.
- **Fix:**
  - `pow(Self, Int) -> Self` plus `pow_mod(Self, exp : Self, modulus : Self) -> Self` (documented to return a value in [0, m)).
  - `to_be_bytes(min_length? : Int)` / `from_be_bytes(BytesView, negative? : Bool)`, or a two's-complement pair.
  - Define and document `ctz(0)`.
- **Source:** me. Codex contributed the `length` label.
