title: [P1-27] Numeric conversions: settle x.to_T() vs T::from_* (Float/Int16 layering)
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-27**, Part 1 (Numerics). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**Conversion spelling now frozen by layering**: E4059 forbids methods on foreign types, so conversions into `Float`/`Int16` can only be `T::from_*`, while everything else is `x.to_T()`. Proposal: move `Int16`/`Float` into builtin; deprecate the Wasm-named duplicates (`convert_uint`, `extend_uint`, `trunc_double`, `Double::from_int`, `Int64::from_int`). Parity matrix in the report. [numerics:53]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### numerics-3 — Conversion spelling: the E4059 rule now freezes the split, and the matrix still has holes
_High · API · breaking to fix: deprecate-then-remove · from the [`numerics` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620747252)_

- **What changed since #4272:**
  - The compiler now rejects methods defined outside the type's package (error 4059; commit 6d7d2e5df removed `Int::to_be_bytes`, `UInt16::reinterpret_as_int16` and others).
  - Same-width signed/unsigned casts were consolidated: `Int::to_uint`, `UInt::to_int`, `Int64::to_uint64` and `UInt64::to_int64` are deprecated in favour of `reinterpret_as_*`. That part is good.
  - The direction of a conversion is now dictated by layering. If the target is `Int16`, `Float` or `BigInt` (all above builtin), the conversion can only be `Target::from_source`. Otherwise it is `source.to_target()`. `UInt16` is in builtin but `Int16` is not, so the asymmetry has no semantic reason.
- **Parity matrix today** (from the live mbti; Y = live, dep = deprecated, - = absent):

  | op | Int | UInt | Int64 | UInt64 | Int16 | UInt16 | Byte | BigInt | Double | Float | Bool |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `abs` | Y | - | Y | - | Y | - | - | **-** | Y | Y | - |
  | `min`/`max`/`clamp` | Y | Y | Y | **-** | **-** | **-** | **-** | - | Y | Y | - |
  | `clz` | Y | Y | Y | Y | **-** | **-** | **-** | (bit_length) | - | - | - |
  | `ctz` / `popcnt` | Y/Y | Y/Y | Y/Y | Y/Y | **-/-** | **-/-** | -/Y | Y/- | - | - | - |
  | `shl`/`shr` method | dep | dep | dep | dep | Y | Y | Y | Y | - | - | - |
  | `to_string(radix?)` | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | **no radix, prints `b'\xFF'`** | Y | Y | Y | Y |
  | `to_be_bytes`/`to_le_bytes` | - | - | - | Y | - | - | - | (`to_octets`) | hidden | Y | - |
  | `until` | Y | - | Y | - | - | - | - | - | dep | dep | - |
  | `to_byte` | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | · | - | - | - | **-** |
  | `to_int` | · | dep | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y |
  | `to_uint` | dep | · | **-** | Y | **-** | Y | Y | Y | Y | **-** | Y |
  | `to_int64` | Y | Y | · | dep | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | **-** | Y |
  | `to_uint64` | Y | Y | dep | · | **-** | Y | Y | Y | Y | **-** | Y |
  | `to_double` | Y | Y | Y | Y | **-** | **-** | Y | **-** | · | Y | - |
  | into Int16 | `Int16::from_int` | **-** | `from_int64` | **-** | · | `reinterpret_from_uint16` | `from_byte` | `to_int16` | **-** | **-** | - |
  | into Float | `Float::from_int` | `from_uint` | `from_int64` | `from_uint64` | **-** | **-** | `from_byte` | - | `from_double` | · | - |
  | Wasm-named duplicates | | `trunc_double` | | `trunc_double`, `extend_uint` | | | | | `from_int`, `convert_uint`, `convert_uint64` | | |

  `Int64::from_int` duplicates `Int::to_int64`, and `Double::from_int` duplicates `Int::to_double`.
- **Fix (preferred):** Move the declarations of `Int16` and `Float` into builtin, next to `UInt16`. Both are already `#builtin`-declared types (commit cac7e0647). Then `Int::to_int16`, `Int::to_float`, `Double::to_float` and the rest become possible, and the rule becomes simply "`x.to_T()` for value conversions, `x.reinterpret_as_T()` for bit casts".
- **Fix (if the types stay out of builtin):** Document the rule "target-side `T::from_*` when T is outside builtin" and apply it everywhere.

  In either case:
  - Deprecate `Double::from_int`, `Int64::from_int`, `Double::convert_uint`, `Double::convert_uint64`, `UInt64::extend_uint` and the two `trunc_double`s.
  - Fill the bold holes from one generated table.

title: [P1-25] Bytes::to_unchecked_string and Buffer::to_string build invalid Strings
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-25**, Part 1 (Text / regex / json). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**Safe-named APIs build invalid Strings**: `Bytes::to_unchecked_string` (odd length → different result per backend) and `Buffer::to_string` / `Show for Buffer` (reads bytes as unchecked UTF-16LE, so `write_string_utf8("hé")` round-trips as garbage). Violates the valid-UTF-16 contract via the ordinary `Show` path. [builtin:81], [text:49]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### builtin-5 — `Bytes::to_unchecked_string` is a safe-named way to build invalid Strings, with backend-dependent results
_High · API · breaking to fix: deprecate-then-remove · from the [`builtin` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620746235)_

- **Where:** `builtin/bytes.mbt:74-89`: `pub fn Bytes::to_unchecked_string(Bytes, offset? : Int32, length? : Int32) -> String`.
- **What:**
  - It reinterprets raw bytes as UTF-16LE and validates neither alignment nor well-formedness. That breaks the settled "Strings are valid UTF-16" contract from a non-`unsafe_` name.
  - Its labels `offset?`/`length?` match no other range API.
  - It is used 9 times outside builtin (encoding/utf16, encoding/ascii, ...), as an internal fast path.
- **Evidence (verified by test):**
  - `b"abc".to_unchecked_string().length()` is 2 on js and native but 1 on wasm-gc.
  - `b"\x00\xd8".to_unchecked_string()` yields a lone surrogate on every backend.
- **Fix:** rename to `Bytes::unsafe_to_string(start~, end~)`, `#doc(hidden)`, with a documented UTF-16LE, even-length, well-formed precondition. Deprecate the old name. Point users at `@encoding/utf16.decode`.
- **Source:** both.

### text-3 — `Buffer::to_string` / `Show for Buffer` build invalid Strings and mis-decode the buffer's own text
_High · Bug · breaking to fix: deprecate-then-remove · from the [`text` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620746724)_

- **Where:**
  - `buffer/buffer.mbt:1191-1193`: `pub impl Show for Buffer with fn output(self, logger) { logger.write_string(self.contents().to_unchecked_string()) }`
  - `buffer/extends.mbt:18`: `pub extend Buffer with Show::{to_string}` (promoted).
- **Evidence (verified by test):**
  - `buf.write_string_utf8("hé"); buf.to_string().length()` gives `1`: the 3 UTF-8 bytes are read as UTF-16, and the odd last byte is dropped silently.
  - Writing the bytes `\x00\xD8` and calling `to_string()` returns a 1-unit String whose unit `is_leading_surrogate()`. That is a lone surrogate created through a safe API, which breaks the settled "Strings are valid UTF-16" contract.
- **History:** #4272 raised this as an API problem ("to_string … mis-decoding"). It is still open and is in fact a contract-breaking bug.
- **Fix:**
  - Make `Show for Buffer` print the same `b"..."` form as `Bytes` (or remove it), and deprecate the promoted `Buffer::to_string` with `#deprecated(skip_current_package=true)` + `#doc(hidden)`.
  - Users decode explicitly with `@utf8.decode(buf.contents())`.
- **Source:** both.

- [`builtin/bytes.mbt:74-89`](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/blob/0cf74cb9c9e8e0508024e5bd7d600648ce5c3fac/builtin/bytes.mbt#L74-L89)

### text-10 — `ToJson for Bytes`/`BytesView` uses a bespoke `\xNN` string format and allocates a String per non-printable byte
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`text` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620746724)_

- **Where:** `json/to_json.mbt:137-148` (`sb.write_string("\\x"); sb.write_string(byte.to_hex())`) and `json/from_json.mbt:310-340`, which accepts only lowercase hex and printable ASCII.
- **What's wrong:**

  - Once 1.0 ships, changing the wire format breaks every stored document.
- **Fix:** pick base64 (`@base64.encode`) before 1.0, or at least write the two hex digits directly from a table. Add `FromJson for BytesView` too (#4272 item).

title: [P1-22] regex: BytesRegex is half a twin of Regex; MatchResult exposes no offsets
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-22**, Part 1 (Text / regex / json). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**`BytesRegex` is half a twin of `Regex`** (missing 7 methods) and neither `MatchResult` exposes offsets. Settle the string-side names (`find` = first + `find_all`?) before copying. [text:62], [cross-package:150]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### text-4 — `BytesRegex` is not a twin of `Regex`, and neither `MatchResult` exposes offsets
_High · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`text` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620746724)_

- **Where:** `bytes/pkg.generated.mbti` vs `string/pkg.generated.mbti`.

  | operation | `@string.Regex` | `@bytes.BytesRegex` |
  |---|---|---|
  | `T(StringView) raise` | yes (+ deprecated `new`) | yes |
  | `execute(input, last_index?) -> MatchResult?` | yes | yes |
  | `+`, `\|` | yes | yes |
  | `find -> Iter[MatchResult]` (all matches) | yes | **no** |
  | `split -> Iter[View]` | yes | **no** |
  | `replace_by(…, limit?)` | yes | **no** |
  | `repeat(min?, max?, greedy?)` | yes | **no** |
  | `capture(String)` | yes | **no** |
  | literal matcher `Regex::string` | yes | **no** |
  | `unsafe_from_string` (panicking) | yes | **no** |
  | `MatchResult::{before, after, content, group, named_group}` | yes | yes |
  | `MatchResult` start/end offsets | **no** | **no** |

- **What's wrong:**
  - A user who wants all matches in a `Bytes` has to write the loop by hand. The only way to resume after a match is the workaround that both doc examples teach: `next = m.before().length() + m.content().length()` (`bytes/regex.mbt:198`, `string/regex.mbt:321`).
  - Neither result type gives match or group spans, the group count, or the group names.
  - The string-side names are themselves undecided in #4272:
    - `find` returns *all* matches while `execute` returns the first;
    - `Regex::string` builds a literal;
    - `unsafe_from_string` only panics;
    - `capture`/`named_group` take `String`;
    - the `replace_by` callback has no `raise?`;
    - the label is `last_index~` rather than `start~`.
  - Copying those names to bytes now would double the later breakage.
- **Fix:**
  1. Decide the shared vocabulary first, for example `find(input, start?) -> MatchResult?` (renamed from `execute`), `find_all -> Iter[MatchResult]`, `split`, `replace_by(…) raise?`, `literal(View)`, `repeat`, `capture(StringView)`. Drop `unsafe_from_string` (the `re"…"`/`reb"…"` literals are the panicking path) or rename it to `Regex::must`.
  2. Add `MatchResult::start() -> Int`, `end() -> Int` and `group_span(Int) -> (Int, Int)?`, with offsets relative to the searched view.
  3. Implement the whole set on both types.
- **Source:** both.

### cross-package-15 — `BytesRegex` is a partial copy of `Regex`, and `@bytes.BytesRegex` stutters
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: no · from the [`cross-package` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620751625)_

- where: `bytes/pkg.generated.mbti:14` has ctor, `execute`, `add`, `lor`; `string/pkg.generated.mbti` `Regex` also has `capture`, `find`, `repeat`, `replace_by`, `split`, `string`, `unsafe_from_string`. Both constructors `raise` untyped `Error`.

### mutable-collections-9 — `List::compare` is lexicographic; every other sequence `Compare` is shortlex
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`mutable-collections` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620747729)_

title: [P1-19] capacity: entries vs buckets differ between constructor and getter, and across maps
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-19**, Part 1 (Collections). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**`capacity` units**: builtin `Map(capacity=)` counts entries but `Map::capacity()` counts buckets; HashMap/HashSet/Set count buckets at different load factors. [builtin:108], [mutable-collections:88]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### builtin-7 — `Map::capacity()` and `Map(capacity=)` use different units
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: deprecate-then-remove · from the [`builtin` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620746235)_

- **Where:**
  - `builtin/linked_hash_map.mbt:109-127`: the constructor doc says `capacity` reserves *entries*, and `Map::capacity()` "reports the bucket count".
  - `builtin/linked_hash_map.mbt:752-757`: `pub fn[K, V] Map::capacity(Self[K, V]) -> Int32` returns buckets.
- **What:**
  - `Array::capacity` counts elements, and Rust's `HashMap::capacity` counts usable entries. Here the same word means two things on one type.
  - The doc admits it, so a caller cannot use `capacity() - length()` as "room before growth".
  - Verified: `Map([], capacity=10).capacity()` is 16. The grow threshold is 13/16 of the bucket count (`calc_grow_threshold`, line 714).
- **Fix:** make `capacity()` return `grow_at` (usable entries). If the bucket count is needed, name it `bucket_count()` and mark it `#doc(hidden)`. Mirror the change in `@hashmap`.
- **Source:** codex (confirmed by reading and test).

### mutable-collections-5 — `capacity?` means entries on Map but buckets on HashMap, HashSet and Set, at three different load factors
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`mutable-collections` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620747729)_

- **Where**:
  - `builtin/linked_hash_map.mbt:109`: Map, "reserves room for at least that many total entries", since `1f0b1739b`.
  - `hashmap/hashmap.mbt:85`: `capacity.max(capacity_for_length(len))`, buckets, grows at 1/2 full.
  - `hashset/hashset.mbt:43` and `set/linked_hash_set.mbt:124`: buckets, grow at 13/16.
- **What**: The same label on four siblings means different things. A pre-sized `HashMap([], capacity=n)` still rehashes before reaching `n`. HashMap also spends about 1.6x the memory of the others for the same contents (1/2 load factor vs 13/16).
- **Evidence** (verified by test). `capacity=16`, then 16 inserts. `capacity()` before→after: Map 32→32, HashMap 16→32, HashSet 16→32, Set 16→32. Codex computed that HashMap grows on the 9th insert and the sets on the 14th.
- **Fix**: Make every `capacity?` an entry-count hint, as Map now does. Reuse Map's overflow-safe `capacity_for_length`/`calc_grow_threshold`. Consider moving HashMap to the 13/16 threshold. Results only change when a hint is passed, but that change is silent, so do it before 1.0.
- **Source**: both.

title: [P1-18] Maps: insert verb is set on mutable and add on immutable; merge vs union
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-18**, Part 1 (Collections). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**Map insert verb went opposite ways**: mutable `set`, immutable `add`; `update` only on VectorMap; live `merge` alias next to `union`. [cross-package:145], [immutable-collections:90]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### immutable-collections-7 — Persistent map update vocabulary: `add` versus mutable `set`, `update` only on VectorMap, two union spellings
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: deprecate-then-remove · from the [`immutable-collections` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620748268)_

- **Where:** `HashMap::add`/`SortedMap::add`/`VectorMap::add(Self, K, V) -> Self`, against mutable `HashMap::set`/`SortedMap::set`/`Map::set`. `immut/vector` already uses `Vector::set(Self, Int, A) -> Self` for persistent replacement. `HashMap::union` has a *live* `#alias(merge)`, and `SortedMap::merge` has no `union`. `update` exists only on `VectorMap`.
- **What's wrong:** Moving code between `@hashmap` and `@immut/hashmap` renames every write. On maps `add` reads as "insert if absent", but it replaces. `SortedSet` has two meanings of `add` (insert, and `+` as union). That was flagged in #4272 and is still open.
- **Fix:** Settle the map write verb once, either `set` (matching mutable maps and `Vector::set`) or `add` everywhere, with an `#alias(..., deprecated)` for the other. Give HashMap and SortedMap the VectorMap `update` signature. Pick one live union name per kind (`merge` for maps, `union` for sets) and deprecate the `merge` alias on immutable HashMap.
- Source: both (Codex raised `add` versus `set`; the rest overlaps #4272).

### cross-package-14 — Mutable/immutable map insert verb went opposite ways
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: deprecate-then-remove · from the [`cross-package` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620751625)_

- where: mutable `sorted_map.SortedMap::set` with `#alias(add, deprecated)`; immutable `immut/sorted_map.SortedMap::add` with `#alias(insert, deprecated)`; `immut/hashmap.HashMap::add`, `immut/vector_map.VectorMap::add` vs `Map`/`HashMap::set`. Meanwhile `immut/vector.Vector::set(i, x)` uses `set`. Also `immut/sorted_set.SortedSet::add(Self, A)` (insert) coexists with `impl Add` (`+` = union) — #4272 theme 2, still open.
- fix: decide whether persistent maps use `add` (OCaml style) or `set` (parity with the mutable twin). Parity argues for `set` (with `add` deprecated); the sorted-set `+` conflict should be resolved by dropping `impl Add for immut SortedSet` in favour of `|` like `HashSet`/`Set`.
- Source: me.

## Notes for whoever picks this up

title: [P1-17] Collections: one rule for which duplicate wins in constructors and add
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-17**, Part 1 (Collections). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**Duplicate semantics**: `@immut/hashmap.HashMap([(k,a),(k,b)])` keeps first, everything else keeps last; sets differ similarly; `SortedSet::add` replaces an equal element while every other set keeps it. [immutable-collections:40], [mutable-collections:169]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### mutable-collections-14 — `SortedSet::add` replaces an equal element; every other set and map keeps the existing one
_Low · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`mutable-collections` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620747729)_

- **Where**: `sorted_set/set.mbt:105` ("If the value already exists, it is replaced"; `add_node` overwrites `n.value`). HashSet, Set, Map, HashMap and SortedMap keep the original key (verified by test, using a record that compares equal by `id` only: SortedSet → "new"; HashSet, Set, Map, HashMap, SortedMap keys → "old").
- **Fix**: Keep the existing representative in `SortedSet::add`, to match the others and avoid a write. If replacement is wanted, offer it under a separate name (`replace`).
- **Source**: codex (verified by me).

### immutable-collections-1 — `HashMap(array)` keeps the first duplicate; every other constructor and sibling keeps the last
_High · Bug · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`immutable-collections` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620748268)_

- **Where:** `immut/hashmap/HAMT.mbt:296-310` (`hash_map_from_array_by_add` walks `n-1 → 0`) and `:313-330` (bulk build with `reverse=true`). `from_iter` (`:916-939`) walks forwards. mbti: `pub fn[K : Eq + Hash, V] HashMap::HashMap(ArrayView[(K, V)]) -> Self[K, V]`.
- **What's wrong:** The same pairs give different maps depending on how they were passed in. `immut/sorted_map` `SortedMap(..)` (compaction keeps `array[end].1`), `immut/vector_map` `VectorMap(..)`, and mutable `hashmap` (which documents last-wins at `hashmap/hashmap.mbt:48`) all keep the last value. The sets behave the same way for representatives: `HashSet(arr)` and `SortedSet(arr)` keep the *last* of a group of equal elements (`immutable_set.mbt` `sorted_set_from_array_by_add` walks backwards, and `compact` and `dedupe` keep `[end]`), while `from_iter` keeps the first. That difference is only observable when `Eq` ignores some fields.
- **Evidence (verified by test):**
  `(HashMap([(1,"first"),(1,"last")]).get(1), from_iter(..).get(1), HashMap(100 pairs, keys i%50).get(0), from_iter(same).get(0))`
  → `(Some("first"), Some("last"), Some(0), Some(50))`. SortedMap gives `(Some("last"), Some("last"))`. VectorMap gives `[(1,"last"),(2,"x")]`.
- **Fix:** Make `HashMap(arr)` and the bulk build last-wins: walk forwards in `_by_add` and use `reverse=false` in `hash_map_from_array`. Document "later pairs override earlier ones" on every map constructor. For sets, decide whether the first or last representative survives, document it, and make `T(arr)` and `from_iter` agree.
- Source: both (I found it; Codex also flagged it and extended it to sets).

title: [P1-16] Sorted collections: one API across mutable/immutable SortedMap and SortedSet
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-16**, Part 1 (Collections). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**Sorted collections**: four types (mutable/immutable × map/set), four different APIs. SortedSet lacks `first`/`last`/`pop_*`/nearest-key/`rev_iter`/`range_bounds`/`retain`; immut SortedMap/Set lack the ordered-query API; `range` is positional + `Iter2`-only and #4333 copied it into more methods. Settle once. [mutable-collections:53,70], [immutable-collections:49]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### mutable-collections-3 — SortedSet lags far behind SortedMap after #4333
_High · API · breaking to fix: no · from the [`mutable-collections` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620747729)_

- **Where**: `sorted_set/pkg.generated.mbti`. SortedMap now has:
  - `first`, `last`, `pop_first`, `pop_last`;
  - `first_ge`, `first_gt`, `last_le`, `last_lt`;
  - `rev_iter`, `rev_iter2`, `rev_keys`, `rev_values`;
  - `rev_range`, `range_bounds(@cmp.Bound, @cmp.Bound)`, `rev_range_bounds`.

  SortedSet has none of these. It also still lacks `retain`, `filter`, `union_in_place`, `add_and_check`, `remove_and_check` and the `BitOr`/`BitAnd`/`BitXOr`/`Sub` operators, all of which HashSet and Set have.
- **What**: The minimum of a SortedSet is `s.iter().next()`; the maximum is a full scan with `s.iter().last()`. Removing the minimum takes two tree walks. Code cannot move between `HashSet` and `SortedSet` by changing only the type. The ordered-collection story is now split between map and set inside one batch.
- **Fix**: Mirror SortedMap's navigation on SortedSet with element types:
  - `first() -> V?`, `last() -> V?`, `pop_first() -> V?`, `pop_last() -> V?`;
  - `first_ge`/`first_gt`/`last_le`/`last_lt(V) -> V?`;
  - `rev_iter() -> Iter[V]`, `rev_range(V, V)`, `range_bounds(@cmp.Bound[V], @cmp.Bound[V]) -> Iter[V]`, `rev_range_bounds`.

  Add `retain((V) -> Bool)`, `filter((V) -> Bool raise?) -> Self raise?`, `union_in_place`, `add_and_check`, `remove_and_check`, and `impl BitOr/BitAnd/BitXOr/Sub` with promoted `lor`/`land`/`lxor`/`sub`. All are additive.
- **Source**: me.

### mutable-collections-4 — `range` family: positional bounds and `Iter2`-only results, now copied into four methods
_High · API · breaking to fix: deprecate-then-remove · from the [`mutable-collections` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620747729)_

- **Where**:
  - `sorted_map`:
    - `range(Self, K, K) -> Iter2[K, V]`
    - `rev_range(Self, K, K) -> Iter2[K, V]`
    - `range_bounds(Self, @cmp.Bound[K], @cmp.Bound[K]) -> Iter2[K, V]`
    - `rev_range_bounds(..) -> Iter2[K, V]`
  - `sorted_set`: `range(Self, V, V) -> Iter[V]`.
  - immut siblings: `range(low~ : K, high~ : K)`.

  Meanwhile `SortedMap::iter`/`rev_iter` return `Iter[(K, V)]`, with separate `iter2`/`rev_iter2`.
- **What**: The #4272 item is still open and #4333 widened it. The new bounded methods also take two positional same-typed bounds. Every whole-map traversal comes as an `Iter`/`Iter2` pair, but every range traversal is `Iter2` only. Moving between `@sorted_map` and `@immut/sorted_map` still breaks every `range` call.
- **Fix**:
  - Before 1.0, pick one shape for all four sorted types. Suggested: `range(low? : Bound[K] = Unbounded, high? : Bound[K] = Unbounded) -> Iter[(K, V)]` plus `range2 -> Iter2`, or document Iter2 as the range convention and add `Iter`-returning twins.
  - Deprecate positional `range(K, K)` via a new name. `range_bounds` could become that labelled `range`.
  - At minimum, give the immut types `range_bounds` and give the mutable ones labelled bounds.
- **Source**: me.

### immutable-collections-2 — Immutable `SortedMap` and `SortedSet` lack the ordered-query vocabulary that mutable `sorted_map` now has
_High · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`immutable-collections` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620748268)_

- **Where:**
  - Mutable `sorted_map/pkg.generated.mbti`: `first`/`last -> (K, V)?`, `first_ge`/`first_gt`/`last_le`/`last_lt`, `pop_first`/`pop_last`, `rev_iter`/`rev_iter2`, `rev_range`, `range_bounds(@cmp.Bound[K], @cmp.Bound[K])`, `rev_range_bounds`, and `keys() -> Iter[K]` with `keys_as_iter` as a deprecated alias.
  - Immutable `sorted_map`: none of these. `#deprecated SortedMap::keys -> Array[K]` sits next to live `keys_as_iter` (`deprecated.mbt`). `split` exists but is private (`map.mbt:207`). There is no `update`, `merge_with`, `intersection` or `difference`.
  - Immutable `sorted_set`: `min`/`max(Self) -> A` (abort), `min_option`/`max_option`, `remove_min` (aborts on empty, and has no `remove_max`). `range(low~, high~)` is inclusive-only, with no exclusive or unbounded form and no `range_bounds`.
- **What's wrong:** This is exactly the API a persistent ordered map exists for, and the mutable sibling has now set the names. Adding methods later is non-breaking. Two things are not: flipping `keys` to return an iterator, and settling `min`/`first` names and abort-versus-Option semantics.
- **Fix:**
  - Immutable `SortedMap`: add `first`/`last`/`first_ge`/`first_gt`/`last_le`/`last_lt -> (K, V)?`, `rev_iter`/`rev_iter2`, `range_bounds`/`rev_range_bounds`, `split(K) -> (Self, V?, Self)` (already written, just private), `update(K, (V?) -> V? raise?) -> Self raise?`, and `remove_first`/`remove_last -> Self` (or `pop_first -> ((K, V), Self)?`). Flip `keys` to `Iter[K]` and make `keys_as_iter` an `#alias(..., deprecated)`.
  - Immutable `SortedSet`: add `first`/`last -> A?`, deprecate `min`/`max`/`min_option`/`max_option` toward them, and add `remove_max`, `range_bounds` and the `*_ge`/`*_le` family.
- Source: me (Codex flagged the `range_bounds`/split part).

title: [P1-15] JS: views over a mutated Array are type-unsound
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-15**, Part 1 (Collections). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**JS views over a mutated Array are type-unsound** (`undefined` as `T`); `MutArrayView` writes after growth reach the array only on JS. [builtin:59]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### builtin-3 — On JS, views over a mutated Array are type-unsound and diverge from native/wasm-gc
_High · Bug · breaking to fix: no · from the [`builtin` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620746235)_

- **Where:**
  - `builtin/arrayview.mbt:23` (the header comment acknowledges it)
  - `builtin/arraycore_js.mbt` (Array = JS array, and views alias the array object itself)
  - `builtin/mutarrayview.mbt:251` (`Array::mut_view` wraps `self.buffer()`)
- **What:** a view taken before `clear`/`truncate`/`pop` keeps its length. On JS, indexing it returns `undefined` at type `T`. A `MutArrayView` taken before growth writes into the live array on JS, but into the detached old buffer on native and wasm-gc.
- **Evidence (verified by test):**
  - `let r = [1,2,3]; let rv = r[0:3]; r.clear(); println(rv[2])`: js **`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`**; native and wasm-gc print the stale `3`.
  - `let v = arr.mut_view(); push x100; v[0] = 42; arr[0]`: js `42`; native and wasm-gc `1`.
- **Fix:** on JS, `ArrayView::at`/`MutArrayView::at`/`set` and iteration should also check `index + start < buf.length` and abort. Do this at least for the safe accessors; the unsafe ones can skip it. Document the cross-backend contract as "a view of an Array is invalidated by any length-changing operation; using it is unspecified but memory-safe". Related: #2195.
- **Source:** both.

title: [P1-14] Document a mutation-during-callback contract for all containers
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-14**, Part 1 (Collections). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**Mutation-during-callback contract**: no container documents traversal invalidation; tree `each` silently skips. (The Array `retain` half is P0-12 / #4596; its audit text about map `update` callbacks is stale, they became `raise?` on Nov 3.) [builtin:72], [mutable-collections:118]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### builtin-4 — `Array::retain` / `retain_map` / `extract_if` corrupt the array when the `raise?` callback raises
_High · Bug · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`builtin` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620746235)_

- **Where:** `builtin/array.mbt` (`retain` ~1249, `retain_map` ~1538, `extract_if` ~1887). The mbti signatures are `pub fn[T] Array::retain(Self[T], (T) -> Bool raise?) -> Unit raise?` and the like.
- **Evidence (verified by test):** `[1,2,3].retain(x => if x == 3 { fail("boom") } else { x == 2 })`, with the error caught, leaves `[2, 2, 3]` on js, wasm-gc and native. The fix in #4282 was closed unmerged.
- **Fix:** merge #4596, which removes `raise?` from the five in-place Array ops. It is source-breaking, so it must land before 1.0.
  - Its audit text says "mutable map update callbacks are also already non-raising". That is now stale: `Map::update`/`get_or_init`/`update_or_default` became `raise?` on 2026-11-03 (b653a3a76, d4347d96f, a79ad7c15).
  - The policy should be written as: bulk in-place ops take non-raising callbacks; single-key updates may raise, because they commit after the callback returns.
- **Source:** codex (known issue; status re-verified).

### mutable-collections-8 — No traversal-invalidation contract on any container; tree `each` silently skips elements
_Medium · Docs · breaking to fix: no · from the [`mutable-collections` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620747729)_

- **Where**: `sorted_map/map.mbt:321` (`each`), `sorted_set/set.mbt:543` (`each`), all `iter`s; the HashMap/HashSet/Set iterators.
- **Evidence** (verified by test): For `SortedMap([(1,1),(2,2),(3,3)])` and `SortedSet([1,2,3])`, `each` with `remove(2)` in the callback visits `[1, 2]`, and 3 is lost. Deletion copies the successor key into the current node.
- **What**: The single-key operations now have carefully written contracts. Builtin Map/HashMap: "may read or write `self`". SortedMap: "must not structurally modify … unspecified results". Traversals have none: no doc, no detection.
- **Fix**: Add one sentence to every `each`/`iter`/`map`/`filter`: "Structurally modifying the collection during traversal has unspecified results (memory-safe)". With the two High fixes above, "memory-safe" becomes true. Optionally add a cheap modification counter checked in `next()` on debug builds.
- **Source**: both (the SortedMap/SortedSet skip came from Codex; verified by me).

title: [P1-13] path: / and join collapse .. lexically and never replace on an absolute right-hand side
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-13**, Part 1 (path). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**`/` and `join` collapse `..` lexically every call and never replace on an absolute RHS** (`"/a" / "/b"` = `/a/b`; `"C:\a" / "D:\b"` = `C:\a\D:\b`) — opposite of pathlib/Rust; undocumented; symlink-unsafe. Plus Win32 namespace-root mangling (`\\?\C:\` → `\\?\C:`). [path:31,44]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### path-2 — `/` and `join` normalize `..` lexically on every call and never replace with an absolute right-hand side; neither hazard is documented as such
_High · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`path` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620751109)_

- **Where:** `path/path.mbt:121-150`; `path/internal/posix/path.mbt:116-127`; `win32/path.mbt:216-238`.
- **What:**
  - **Lexical `..` on every join.** `Path("base/link") / "../file"` becomes `base/file`. If `link` is a symlink, the OS resolves `base/link/../file` somewhere else. Rust `Path::join` and Python `pathlib`'s `/` deliberately don't collapse `..`. Go's `filepath.Join` does, and its `Clean` documents the symlink caveat. No doc in `path` mentions symlinks: grepping `symlink|lexical` finds only the garbled "cwd is already resolve symbolic link" warning on `resolve` and `relative`.
  - **Absolute right side is appended, not substituted.** `Path("/a") / "/b"` is `/a/b`; on Windows, `"C:\\a" / "D:\\b"` is `C:\a\D:\b`. Python's `/`, which the operator borrows from, and Rust's `join` both return `/b`.
  - **Windows drive-relative.** `Path("C:") / "foo"` becomes `C:\foo`, which turns a drive-relative path into a rooted one. Rust gives `C:foo`.
- **Evidence:** verified by test against Node. `join("a/","../..")` is `".."`, `join("/a","/b")` is `/a/b`, win32 `join("C:","foo")` is `C:\foo` and `join("C:\\a","D:\\b")` is `C:\a\D:\b`, all identical to `node:path`.
- **Fix:**
  - Make `/` and `join` a pure push: no `..` collapsing, absolute or rooted right side replaces (with Windows drive-prefix rules as in Rust). Keep lexical cleanup in `normalize`.
  - Rename `normalize` to `normalize_lexically`, or document the symlink hazard prominently.
  - If Node semantics are kept on purpose, document all three behaviours on `/` itself, and don't use pathlib's operator for a different meaning.
- **Source:** both.

### path-3 — Win32 namespace roots are mangled: `\\?\C:\` resolves to the raw volume `\\?\C:`, and `..` can pop the drive, share or device
_High · Bug · breaking to fix: no · from the [`path` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620751109)_

- **Where:** `win32/path.mbt:279-297` (`is_regular_win_root` excludes `VerbatimRoot`/`DeviceRoot`); `win_path.mbt:244-279,214-232` (everything after `\\?\` goes into the ordinary component stack); the wrong expectation is pinned at `win32/path_test.mbt:463`.
- **What (verified by whitebox test):**
  - `resolve("\\\\?\\C:\\")` returns `\\?\C:`. Opening `\\?\C:` opens the volume device, not the root directory.
  - `normalize("\\\\?\\C:\\..\\x")` returns `\\?\x`.
  - `normalize("\\\\.\\pipe\\..\\x")` returns `\\.\x`.
  - `normalize("\\\\?\\UNC\\srv\\share\\..\\..\\x")` returns `\\?\UNC\x`.

  Node gives the same output for every one. These are Node bugs ported faithfully. Verbatim paths are also normalized at all (forward slashes turned into `\`, `..` collapsed), even though Win32 defines `\\?\` as "no parsing".
- **Fix:**
  - Model the namespace root as part of the prefix: `\\?\C:\`, `\\?\UNC\srv\share\`, `\\.\pipe\`.
  - Clamp `..` at it, and preserve the trailing separator in `trim_resolved_trailing_separators`.
  - Leave verbatim (`\\?\`) paths byte-identical in `normalize`/`join`, as Rust does.
  - The doc contract has to change from "follows Node" to "follows Win32 path rules (Node-compatible except …)". That is cheaper to say before 1.0.
- **Source:** codex (behaviour verified by me, and the Node parity check is mine).

title: [P1-12] path: pub(all) struct Path(String) freezes the representation
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-12**, Part 1 (path). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**`pub(all) struct Path(String)` freezes the representation** (can't become abstract or OS-string-backed; literal sugar `let p : Path = "a"` breaks if made read-only — needs a compiler literal hook). No `Hash`/`Compare`/`ToStringView`; nothing in core consumes `@path` (`@fs` takes `StringView`). Decide: text-only-and-fail-loudly vs abstract + literal trait. [path:16], [cross-package:66]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### path-1 — `pub(all) struct Path(String)` freezes a String-backed, constructible representation that cannot carry non-UTF-8 OS paths
_High · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`path` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620751109)_

- **Where:** `path/path.mbt:33-34`; mbti `pub(all) struct Path(String)`. `internal/os_string/os_string.mbt:19-20,30-32,79-81`. `async/internal/c_buffer/c_buffer.mbt:70-78`.
- **What:**
  - Native POSIX `OsString` is `Bytes`, but its only conversion to `String` is `@utf8.decode_lossy`, and `async/fs` directory entries are decoded the same lossy way (`decode_as_os_string`, `async/fs/dir.mbt:343`).
  - A file named with bytes `FF` cannot be reopened, renamed or deleted by name. Two different non-UTF-8 names collapse to the same `"\u{FFFD}"`, so `rmdir(recursive=true)` or `walk` operate on the wrong name.
  - On Windows, `OsString(String)` admits unpaired surrogates (its own doc comment, `os_string.mbt:18-20`), which violates the settled "Strings are valid UTF-16" contract at the FFI boundary.
  - With the field public (`path.0`) and `Path(...)` constructible by anyone, the String backing is frozen. Rust `OsStr`/`PathBuf` and Node `Buffer` paths are the comparison points.
- **Constraint (verified by test):** I changed it to `pub struct Path(String)` and the consumer test failed: `let path : @path.Path = "a"` gives `Error [4036] Cannot create values of the read-only type: Path`. The string-literal sugar, and with it `path / "b"`, requires a `pub(all)` constructor. Hiding the representation costs the ergonomics, unless the compiler grows a literal hook for abstract types.
- **Fix:** Choose one, explicitly, before 1.0:
  - (a) Declare `Path` text-only. Document that non-UTF-8 names are unrepresentable, and make `os_string`/`fs` fail instead of decoding lossily, so names never silently alias.
  - (b) Make `Path` abstract (`struct Path { priv repr : String }` or similar) with `Path::from_string(StringView)`, `to_string()`, and later `from_os_bytes`. Ask for a literal-overloading hook, for example an `#literal` / `FromStringLiteral` trait, so `"a" : Path` survives.

  Doing nothing locks in (a) without the fail-loudly part.
- **Source:** both (Codex raised the lossy round-trip; the literal-sugar constraint is mine).

### cross-package-6 — `@path.Path` is a `pub(all)` String newtype that doesn't interoperate with `@fs`
_High · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`cross-package` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620751625)_

- where: `path/pkg.generated.mbti:18` `#derive(Eq, @debug.Debug) pub(all) struct Path(String)`; all 27 path parameters in `async/fs` are `StringView`, results are `String` (`realpath`, `tmpdir`, `readdir`, `walk` callback), `Watcher::Watcher(String, …)` (`async/fs/pkg.generated.mbti:167`), `@process.redirect_from_file(String)`.
- what: (a) `pub(all)` freezes the representation (`.0` access + unchecked construction), so Path can never cache a normalized form or switch to an OS string; `@http.CaseInsensitiveString(String)` and `@process.CancellationHandler(...)` have the same problem while the comparable `@socket.Addr` is opaque. (b) No `Hash`/`Compare`, so `Path` can't key a `Map`/`SortedMap`. (c) No `ToStringView` impl, so every fs call needs `p.to_string()`.
- fix: `pub struct Path` (abstract) with `Path::Path(StringView)`, `as_view()`/`impl ToStringView`, `#derive(Eq, Compare, Hash, Debug)`; decide whether `@fs` accepts `&ToStringView` (non-breaking for `StringView` callers) or `Path`. Same abstraction for `CaseInsensitiveString`.
- Source: both (codex flagged pub(all) wrappers; interop/Hash are mine).

title: [P1-11] async/*: apply the AGENTS.md trait-method promotion policy
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-11**, Part 1 (One concept, one shape (sync/async and sibling packages)). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

### async-io-22 — AGENTS.md promotion policy violations
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: no · from the [`async-io` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620750078)_

- **Where:** `async/socket/deprecated.mbt`, `async/fs/deprecated.mbt`.
- **What's wrong:** policy says `Eq::equal`, `Compare::compare` and `Hash::hash` are promoted on every type that impls them, and operators always are. Violations:
  - `Addr`: `equal`, `compare` and `hash` are deprecated.
  - `FileKind` and `FsEvent`: `equal` is deprecated.
  - `Timestamp`: `equal`, `compare` and **`Sub::sub`** (an operator) are deprecated.
  - Separately, `TlsError::to_string` and `ResolveHostnameError::to_string` are promoted on error types, which have no canonical string representation per policy.
- **Proposed fix:** move `equal`, `compare`, `hash` and `sub` into `pub extend` in `extends.mbt`; keep `not_equal`, `op_*` and `hash_combine` deprecated.

title: [P1-10] Pick one byte-buffer parameter shape and one file-offset type
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-10**, Part 1 (One concept, one shape (sync/async and sibling packages)). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**Byte-buffer parameters in three shapes** (`MutArrayView[Byte]` / `FixedArray`+`offset?`+`max_len?` / `Bytes`+`offset?`+`len?`); file offsets `Int64` in fs vs `UInt64` in zip. [cross-package:103,155]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### cross-package-10 — Caller-supplied byte buffers have three shapes
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: deprecate-then-remove · from the [`cross-package` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620751625)_

- where: sync codecs: `step(BytesView, MutArrayView[Byte])` (flate×2, gzip×2, zlib×2, `EntryReader::step`), `Compressor::compress_into(BytesView, MutArrayView[Byte])`; async reads: `read_into(FixedArray[Byte], offset? : Int32, max_len? : Int32)` (19 types + the `BinaryReader` trait), `RawFd::read`, `UdpClient::recv*`; async writes: `BinaryWriter::write(BytesView)` but `RawFd::write(Bytes, offset?, len?)`, `UdpClient::send(Bytes, offset?, len?)`, `BinaryWriterImpl::raw_write_impl(Bytes, offset~, len~)`; `@fs.File::read_at(FixedArray[Byte], position~, offset?, len?)`.
- what: `MutArrayView[Byte]` (added recently for compress) subsumes `FixedArray + offset + max_len`, and `BytesView` subsumes `Bytes + offset + len`. Because `BinaryReader` is `pub(open)`, the `read_into` shape is the hardest to change after 1.0.
- fix: decide now. Recommended: output = `MutArrayView[Byte]`, input = `BytesView`, everywhere; migrate `read_into(buf : MutArrayView[Byte])` with the old shape kept as a deprecated default method on the trait. If async keeps `FixedArray` for FFI reasons, document it as the async-only rule.
- Source: me.

### cross-package-16 — Byte offsets and sizes: `Int64` in fs, `UInt64` in zip, `Int32` in zip limits
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: no · from the [`cross-package` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620751625)_

title: [P1-9] async/compress: unify label spellings and use one duration type
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-9**, Part 1 (One concept, one shape (sync/async and sibling packages)). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**Label spellings** across async/compress: `allow_exist?`/`allow_existing?`, `max_concurrent?`/`max_concurrency?`, `max_output?`/`max_output_bytes?` (Int32 vs UInt64), `size?`/`capacity?`/`size_hint?`, `end`/`finish`. **Durations** are bare `Int32` ms under five names. [cross-package:72,92]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### cross-package-7 — Label spellings diverge in async/compress (table)
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: deprecate-then-remove · from the [`cross-package` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620751625)_

| concept | spellings (package: signature) | canonical |
|---|---|---|
| "ok if it already exists" | `allow_existing?` (`@fs.create`, :20), `allow_exist?` (`@fs.mkdir`, :30) | `allow_existing?` |
| concurrency cap | `max_concurrent?` (`@async.all`/`any`), `max_concurrency?` (`@fs.walk`, :56) | `max_concurrency?` |
| output byte cap | `max_output? : Int32` (flate×3, gzip, zlib), `max_output_bytes? : Int32` (`@zip.write`, shell×2), `max_output_bytes? : UInt64` (`EntryReadLimits`), error payload `limit~ : UInt64` | `max_output_bytes? : Int` everywhere, payload same type |
| buffer pre-allocation | `capacity?` (Array, Map, Deque, HashMap, HashSet, Queue, Set — 7), `size_hint?` (Buffer, StringBuilder), `size?` (`@io.BufferedWriter::new`, which also exposes `capacity()`) | `capacity?` (keep `size_hint?` only on `Iter::new`, where it is an estimate) |
| partial-read length | `max_len?` (19 `read_into`s), `len?` (`File::read_at`, :104 — same semantics as `read_into`) | `max_len?` on reads, `len?` on writes |
| per-entry/part length | `len~` (blit_to, range_equal), `len?` (Array::blit_to, Deque::drain), `length?` (Bytes::to_unchecked_string, BigInt::to_octets), `count?` (quickcheck, bench) | `len` for slices, `count` for repetitions |
| headers | `headers?` vs `extra_headers?` (semantic: base vs extra — fine) | keep |
| argv | `Command::parse(argv? : ArrayView)` vs `Command::parse_outcome(argv~ : ArrayView)` (argparse) | both `argv?` |

title: [P1-7] compress: unify naming across flate, gzip and zlib
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-7**, Part 1 (One concept, one shape (sync/async and sibling packages)). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**compress family has three naming schemes**: flate `deflate_all`/`inflate_exact`/`Incremental*` vs gzip/zlib `compress`/`decompress`/`Encoder`/`Decoder`; trailing-garbage handling differs; no `consumed` count; `strategy?` vs `level?`. [net-compress:175], [cross-package:109]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### net-compress-7 — The three codec packages use three naming schemes and have different capabilities (parity table)
_High · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`net-compress` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620750602)_

| concept | `@flate` | `@gzip` | `@zlib` | `async/gzip` | `@zip` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| one-shot encode | `deflate_all(in, strategy?, dictionary?, fast_store?)` | `compress(in, strategy?, fast_store?)` | `compress(in, strategy?, dictionary?, fast_store?)` | — | `write(archive, preserve?, max_output_bytes?, level?, fast_store?)` |
| one-shot decode | `inflate_exact` **and** `inflate_prefix(.., max_output?, cancelled?, two_pass?)` | `decompress(in, max_output?, cancelled?)` — trailing bytes **silently ignored**, no `consumed`, no `two_pass` | `decompress(in, dictionary?, max_output?, cancelled?)` — trailing bytes **rejected**, no `consumed`, no `two_pass` | — | `read_all(bytes, limits?, cancelled?)` |
| reusable whole-buffer | `Compressor` / `Decompressor` (+`*_into`) | — | — | — | — |
| streaming encoder | `IncrementalEncoder(level?, dictionary?, fast_store?)`, `reset(dictionary?)` | `Encoder(level?, fast_store?)`, `reset()` | `Encoder(level?, dictionary?, fast_store?)`, `reset(dictionary?)` | `Encoder[W](W, mtime?, extra_flags?, operating_system?)` — no level | `Writer(sink, level?, fast_store?)` |
| streaming decoder | `IncrementalDecoder(dictionary?)`: `step/reset/is_finished`; no `check_end`/`unused_input` | `Decoder(multistream?)`: `step/check_end/unused_input/is_finished`; **no `reset`** | `Decoder(dictionary?)`: same; **no `reset`** | `Decoder[R](R)`; single member | `EntryReader::step -> EntryStep` + `last_produced()` (different result shape) |
| tuning | `Strategy` (one-shot) **vs** `level : Int` (streaming) | same split | same split | none | `level` only |
| header metadata | n/a | cannot set or read mtime/name/OS | n/a | set only, cannot read | dos date/time etc. |
| error kinds | `Corrupt`, `TrailingData`, … | `InvalidDeflate`, `LengthMismatch`, no `TrailingData` | `InvalidDeflate`, `TrailingData` | private `FormatError` | `InvalidDeflate`, `SizeMismatch`, `LimitExceeded(kind~,..)` |
| limit width | `max_output : Int32` / error `UInt64` | same | same | none | `ReadLimits` Int32 fields; `EntryReadLimits`/`DirectoryLimits` UInt64 |

- Verified by test: `@gzip.decompress(g + b"garbage!")` returns OK.
  `@zlib.decompress(z + b"garbage!")` raises `TrailingData` with the misleading message
  "data between DEFLATE stream and trailer": zlib assumes the trailer is the last 4 bytes
  (`zlib.mbt:178`). So zlib streams embedded in larger buffers (git packfiles, PDF objects)
  cannot be decoded one-shot at all.
- Fix (pick one vocabulary and apply it everywhere):
  - `@flate.compress/decompress/decompress_prefix`, replacing `deflate_all/inflate_exact/inflate_prefix`.
  - `@gzip`/`@zlib` gain `decompress_prefix(..) -> Decompressed` (data + consumed) and `two_pass?`.
    `@gzip.decompress` becomes exact by default with a `TrailingData` kind, or takes `trailing? : Ignore|Reject` explicitly.
  - Streaming types are `Encoder`/`Decoder` in all three packages, so drop `Incremental`. All three
    get `reset(..)`, `check_end`, `unused_input`.
  - The same `Compressor`/`Decompressor` reusable objects exist in gzip and zlib, or in none.
  - `Strategy` is accepted by the streaming constructors too, or by none (`level` everywhere).
- Source: me (Codex raised the gzip/zlib trailing-data point independently).

### cross-package-11 — Compression family naming and options
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: deprecate-then-remove · from the [`cross-package` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620751625)_

| concept | flate | gzip / zlib | archive/zip | async/gzip | canonical |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| one-shot encode | `deflate_all(strategy?)` | `compress(strategy?)` | `write(level?)` | — | `compress` |
| one-shot decode | `inflate_exact` / `inflate_prefix` | `decompress` | `read_all` | — | `decompress` (+`decompress_prefix`) |
| reusable one-shot object | `Compressor` / `Decompressor` | — | — | — | keep |
| streaming object | `IncrementalEncoder` / `IncrementalDecoder` | `Encoder` / `Decoder` | `Writer` / `EntryReader` | `Encoder` / `Decoder` | `Encoder`/`Decoder` |
| quality knob | `strategy? : Strategy` (one-shot) but `level? : Int32` (streaming) | same split | `level? : Int32` only | none | `strategy? : Strategy` everywhere (`Strategy::Standard(level~)` already exists) |
| finish | `DeflateAction::Finish`, `is_finished` | same | `Writer::finish` | `Encoder::end` | `finish` |
| limit | `max_output?` | `max_output?` | `max_output_bytes?` / `ReadLimits` | none | see label table |
- fix: rename `IncrementalEncoder/Decoder`→`Encoder/Decoder` in flate (alias old), add `strategy?` to every streaming encoder and zip (keep `level?` as shorthand or deprecate), `async/gzip.Encoder::end`→`finish`.
- Source: both (codex: strategy-vs-level and end/finish; rest mine).

title: [P1-6] async/gzip: drop gzip_internal and build on @gzip.Encoder/Decoder
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-6**, Part 1 (One concept, one shape (sync/async and sibling packages)). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**Two gzip implementations**: delete `async/internal/gzip_internal` (2.4k lines, weaker ratio by 46–75%, rejects FNAME, single member, no level, P0-1) and build `async/gzip` + HTTP on `@gzip.Encoder/Decoder::step`. [net-compress:51], [cross-package:33]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### net-compress-2 — `async/gzip` uses a second, weaker DEFLATE engine; rebuild it on `compress/gzip`
_High · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`net-compress` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620750602)_

- Where: `async/gzip/pkg.generated.mbti` (whole package), `async/internal/gzip_internal/*`
  (encoder, decoder, huffman, its own `crc32.mbt`), `async/http/parser.mbt:31`.
- What (all verified by test unless marked):
  - **Rejects gzip members with optional header fields.** `metadata.mbt:74`
    `guard flags is b'\x00' else raise InvalidHeader`. A member with `FLG=FNAME` (the default
    output of the `gzip` CLI, and what nginx `gzip_static` serves) fails with
    `FormatError.InvalidHeader`. `compress/gzip` accepts the same bytes. So `@http.get` of such a
    resource fails.
  - **Single member only.** `async/gzip/decoder.mbt:48` stops at `is_finished()`. In the test the
    decoder finished with the second member left unread. `compress/gzip` defaults to
    `multistream=true`.
  - **Rejects an all-zero distance alphabet** (`huffman.mbt:50` "empty huffman tree" is applied to the
    distance tree at `decoder.mbt:292`). RFC 1951 allows this. It also accepts incomplete trees
    (never checks `left == 0`). From reading.
  - **Toy encoder:** 1 KiB window, max match 64, fixed Huffman only (`encoder.mbt:15-47`), no
    `level`. On a 1.7 MB JSON-lines corpus: async gzip = 198,702 bytes, `@gzip.compress`
    level 1 = 135,776, level 6 = 113,663. That is 46-75% larger.
  - **Errors are a private `FormatError`** (`metadata.mbt:17`). `gzip_internal`'s mbti lists no
    errors and `async/gzip` re-exports none, so callers cannot match on them.
    `@gzip.GzipError(GzipErrorKind, String)` already exists.
  - Encoder options diverge from `@gzip.Encoder`: async has `mtime?/extra_flags?/operating_system?`
    and no level; sync has `level?/fast_store?` and no header fields.
  - The CRC-32 is a duplicate of `internal/checksum` (slicing-by-8 vs the shared slicing-by-16).
- Fix: delete `async/internal/gzip_internal`. Implement
  `async/gzip.Encoder[W](W, level? : Int, fast_store? : Bool, mtime? : UInt32, os? : Byte)` and
  `Decoder[R](R, multistream? : Bool = true)` as thin `@io` adapters over `@gzip.Encoder::step` /
  `@gzip.Decoder::step/check_end/unused_input`, raising `@gzip.GzipError`. Add header options to
  `@gzip.Encoder` and `@gzip.compress` so the sync and async encoders take the same options.
  HTTP's `Reader` should drive `@gzip.Decoder` directly. `unused_input()` is exactly what the
  HTTP reader needs to hand trailing chunk bytes back.
- Source: both. Codex raised the FNAME, multimember, error-type and empty-distance points; I
  found the duplicate engine, ratio and options, and confirmed FNAME and multimember by test.

### cross-package-3 — Two independent gzip implementations with disjoint option sets
_High · API/Perf · breaking to fix: deprecate-then-remove · from the [`cross-package` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620751625)_

- where: `async/gzip/moon.pkg` imports only `async/io` and `async/internal/gzip_internal` (2,413 lines: `crc32.mbt`, `huffman.mbt`, `decoder.mbt`, `encoder.mbt`), not `compress/gzip`/`compress/flate` (12.5k lines + `internal/checksum`).
  - sync: `compress/gzip` `Encoder::Encoder(level? : Int32, fast_store? : Bool)`, `Decoder::Decoder(multistream? : Bool)`, `decompress(max_output?, cancelled?) raise GzipError`.
  - async: `async/gzip` `Encoder::Encoder(W, mtime? : UInt32, extra_flags? : Byte, operating_system? : Byte)` (no level), `Decoder::Decoder(R)` (no multistream, no output limit), raises untyped errors from `gzip_internal` (`raise InvalidBlock(...)` at `async/internal/gzip_internal/decoder.mbt:286`).
- what: the same format has two codecs that differ in compression ratio, header fields, multistream behaviour and error type; the sync `step(BytesView, MutArrayView[Byte])` API was designed precisely to be driven by an async adapter. Doubles maintenance and the fuzzing surface.
- fix: re-implement `async/gzip.{Encoder,Decoder}` as thin adapters over `@gzip.Encoder::step`/`Decoder::step`, accept the union of options (`level?`, `strategy?`, `fast_store?`, `multistream?`, `max_output?` + the header fields, which should then also be added to the sync `Encoder`), raise `@gzip.GzipError`; delete `gzip_internal`. Public signatures can stay (additive labels) so this is non-breaking for users except the error type.
- Source: me (codex flagged the option mismatch only).

## Code (pinned to `0cf74cb9c`)

- [`async/http/parser.mbt:31`](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/blob/0cf74cb9c9e8e0508024e5bd7d600648ce5c3fac/async/http/parser.mbt#L31)

### numerics-2 — Integer division by zero and `MIN / -1` have no contract and diverge per backend
_High · Bug · breaking to fix: no · from the [`numerics` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620747252)_

- **Where:** Every fixed-width `Div`/`Mod` impl: `Int::div` = `%i32_div`, Int64, UInt, UInt64. `Int16`, `UInt16` and `Byte` inherit the behaviour because they divide through Int (`int16/int16.mbt` `Div` impl). No doc in builtin or the `@int*` READMEs states the contract. A grep for "division by zero" finds only the Double docs.
- **Evidence:** Verified by test, with the divisor computed at runtime so it cannot be constant-folded, in both debug and `--release`.

  | expr | native (arm64) | js | wasm-gc |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `10 / 0` | **0** | throws bare `Error` | trap "divide by zero" |
  | `10 % 0` | **10** | throws | trap |
  | `9L / 0L`, `9U / 0U`, `UInt64`, `Int16`, `UInt16`, `Byte` `/ 0` | **0** | throws | trap |
  | `Int::MIN / -1`, `Int64::MIN / -1` | wraps to MIN | wraps to MIN | trap "divide result unrepresentable" |
  | `Int16::MIN / -1` | -32768 | -32768 | -32768 |

  `BigInt` panics with "division by zero" everywhere. On x86-64 native the C code would raise SIGFPE instead. So silent 0 is what arm64 hardware happens to do, not a MoonBit semantic.
- **Fix:** Specify the semantics: `/` and `%` by zero panic with a message on every backend, and `MIN / -1` wraps (`MIN % -1 == 0`). Native and wasm-gc need a compiler-emitted check. The bare js `Error` should become the normal MoonBit panic. Document the rule once in the builtin `Int` docs and in the `@int` README.
- **Source:** me.

title: [P1-3] argparse, regex, shell, async/gzip: replace untyped or private errors with public typed errors
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-3**, Part 1 (Errors). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**Untyped/private errors**: argparse (`Failed(Error)` wrapping private `Message(String)`; `ParseOutcome` is `pub(all)`), regex constructors raise internal `ParserError`, `@shell` error type private, `async/gzip` raises private `gzip_internal` errors. [tooling:14], [text:97], [async-io:221]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### text-5 — Regex constructors raise an error type users can't name
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: no · from the [`text` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620746724)_

- **Where:**
  - `string/regex.mbt:70`: `pub fn Regex::Regex(StringView) -> Self raise`
  - `bytes/regex.mbt:53`: `BytesRegex::BytesRegex(StringView) -> Self raise`
  - The real error is `suberror ParserError { ParserError(at~ : Int32, hint~ : String) }` in `string/internal/regex_parser/parser_error.mbt:16-18`, which is internal (and duplicated under `bytes/internal/regex_parser`).
- **Evidence (verified by test):** `Regex("a(")` raises a value whose Debug is `ParserError(at=1, hint="Unclosed group")`. User code can only call `to_string()` on it, because it cannot match on an internal type.
- **What's wrong:** this is the only parser in the area whose position information is unreachable. JSON exposes `Position` and the codecs expose `Malformed`.
- **Fix:** add a public `pub suberror RegexError { RegexError(offset~ : Int, message~ : String) }` in `@string`. `@bytes` can re-export it with `pub using` if a dependency is acceptable, or define a twin. Narrow both signatures to `raise RegexError`. Narrowing an error type does not break callers.
- **Source:** both.

### tooling-1 — argparse failures are an untyped `Error` wrapping a private `Message(String)`
_High · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`tooling` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620748867)_

- **Where**: `argparse/pkg.generated.mbti`: `pub(all) enum ParseOutcome { ...; Failed(Error) }`, `Command::parse(...) -> Matches raise`. `argparse/error.mbt:21` `priv suberror ArgError { Message(String) }`. The structured variants exist but are private: `error.mbt:60` `priv suberror ArgParseError { UnknownArgument(String, String?); MissingValue(String); MissingRequired(..); TooFewValues(..); ... }`. `parser.mbt:254-336` flattens every one of them, and `ArgBuildError::Unsupported`, into `ArgError::Message(text)`.
- **What's wrong**: The only thing a caller can do with a failure is `to_string()`. A usage error (exit code 2 by convention, print usage) and a bad command definition (a programmer bug) have the same type. Only the text prefix differs: `error: command definition validation failed: ...` versus `error: unexpected argument ...`. `ParseOutcome` is `pub(all)` with `Failed(Error)`, so narrowing the payload after 1.0 is a breaking change. `parse` also falls back to `println(err.to_string()); panic()` for any error it does not recognise (`command.mbt` `Command::parse`).
- **Evidence**: verified by test. `Command("demo", flags=[FlagArg("x", long="x"), FlagArg("x", long="y")]).parse_outcome(argv=[])` gives `Failed(e)` with the text `error: command definition validation failed: duplicate arg name: x`. `Command("demo").parse_outcome(argv=["--nope"])` gives `Failed(e)` with the text `error: unexpected argument '--nope' found\n\nUsage: ...`. Nothing other than the string tells the two apart.
- **Fix**: Add a public error type: `pub suberror ArgParseError { Usage(kind~ : UsageError, message~ : String); InvalidCommand(String) }` with `pub enum UsageError { UnknownArgument(String, hint~ : String?); MissingValue(String); MissingRequired(String, required_by~ : String?); TooFewValues(..); TooManyValues(..); TooManyPositionals(..); InvalidValue(String); MissingGroup(String); GroupConflict(String) }`. Its Show should give the current display text. Then change the signatures to `Failed(ArgParseError)` and `Command::parse(...) -> Matches raise ArgParseError`, and make `ParseOutcome` `pub` (read-only) instead of `pub(all)`. This also answers the cross-cutting "typed parse errors vs `Failure`" question for argparse: typed.
- Source: both (codex #4)

### async-io-19 — `@shell`: private error type, lossy stderr, vocabulary diverges from `@process`
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: yes · from the [`async-io` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620750078)_

- **Where:** `async/shell/output.mbt:86` (`priv suberror ShellError { …, OutputLimitExceeded, CommandFailed(Output) }`); `output.mbt:21-26` (stderr stored only as lossy `String`); `execute.mbt:619`.
- **What's wrong:**
  - Callers of `Cmd::run` / `Output::check` cannot match on `CommandFailed` to get the status or output back, nor tell a limit-exceeded error from a configuration error.
  - Binary stderr is unrecoverable.
  - Naming vs `@process`:

    | `@shell` | `@process` |
    |---|---|
    | `Capture` | `Collect` |
    | `AppendToFile` | `AppendFile` |
    | `env?` | `extra_env?` |
    | `cwd? : String` | `cwd? : StringView` |
    | `Output::exit_code()` method | `ProcessResult.exit_code` field |
    | `stdout()` / `stdout_bytes()` (lossy) | `stdout_text() raise` / `stdout_binary()` |

  - `Output` collides with `@stdio.Output`.
  - NUL handling differs: shell rejects embedded NUL, but `@process` silently skips env keys containing NUL and truncates values (`process/unix.mbt:40-43`).
  - README signature shows `Array[String]`; the code takes `ArrayView[String]`.
- **Proposed fix:**
  - `pub suberror ShellError` with `#non_exhaustive`, and add `Output::stderr_bytes()`.
  - Align vocabulary with `@process`: one word for collect/capture, one for append, one env label.
  - Rename `Output` to `CmdOutput`.
  - Make `@process` reject NUL (raise) the way shell does.
- **Source:** both (private error and stderr bytes: codex, verified; naming and NUL: me)

title: [P1-2] compress/zip: codec errors lack Show/Debug/Eq and use different kind names
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-2**, Part 1 (Errors). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**Codec errors (`InflateError`, `GzipError`, `ZlibError`, `ZipError`) have no `Show`/`Debug`/`Eq`**; kind names differ per package. [cross-package:20], [net-compress:204]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### net-compress-8 — Codec error types have no `Show`/`Debug`; error kinds disagree between packages
_Medium · API · breaking to fix: no · from the [`net-compress` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620750602)_

- Where: `compress/flate/pkg.generated.mbti` `pub suberror InflateError { InflateError(InflateErrorKind, String) }`,
  and the same for `GzipError`, `ZlibError`, `ZipError`. None derive anything. (http/websocket
  errors do derive `Debug`.)
- What (verified by test): `"\{e}"` on any of them, viewed as `Error`, prints only
  `moonbitlang/core/compress/flate.InflateError.InflateError`. The kind and the diagnostic message
  are lost. Interpolating the typed error does not compile ("does not implement trait Show").
  Kind names drift for the same condition: `Corrupt` (flate) vs `InvalidDeflate`
  (gzip/zlib/zip); `LengthMismatch` (gzip) vs `SizeMismatch` (zip); `OutputLimitExceeded(limit~,observed~)`
  vs `LimitExceeded(kind~,limit~,observed~)`. All kind enums are `pub(all)`, so adding a variant
  after 1.0 breaks exhaustive matches.
- Fix: derive `Debug` and implement `Show` as `"<pkg>: <kind>: <message>"` on all four. Align kind
  names (`InvalidDeflate` everywhere, or `Corrupt` everywhere; `SizeMismatch` everywhere). Decide
  now whether the kind enums are extensible; if they are, document "match with a wildcard arm".
- Source: me.

### cross-package-1 — Compress/zip error types implement no Show, Debug or Eq
_High · API · breaking to fix: no · from the [`cross-package` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620751625)_

- where: `compress/flate/pkg.generated.mbti:18` `pub suberror InflateError { InflateError(InflateErrorKind, String) }`; same shape `compress/gzip` `GzipError`, `compress/zlib` `ZlibError`, `archive/zip` `ZipError` (`archive/zip/errors.mbt:75`, `compress/gzip/gzip.mbt:54`). No `#derive`, no impls in the mbti.
- what: every other public error type in core has at least `Debug` (encoding `Malformed`, `path.ResolveError`, all async errors) or `Show` (`json.ParseError`, `OsError`). These four cannot be `inspect`ed, `@debug`-printed, or compared in tests unless upcast to `Error`. Their `*Kind` payloads *do* derive `Eq + Debug`, so the omission is clearly accidental.
- evidence (verified by test): a temp test `let r : Result[Bytes, @gzip.GzipError] = try Ok(@gzip.decompress(b"xx")) catch { e => Err(e) }; ... inspect(e)` fails with `Type @moonbitlang/core/compress/gzip.GzipError does not implement trait Show: no impl is defined` (file deleted).
- fix: `#derive(Eq, @debug.Debug)` on all four plus `impl Show` printing `"<kind>: <message>"`; promote `equal`/`to_string` in each `extends.mbt` per policy.
- Source: both.

title: [P1-1] Mark public error/kind enums #non_exhaustive before 1.0
body:
Sub-issue of #4613 — **P1-1**, Part 1 (Errors). From the round-2 pre-1.0 review (#4612).

## Summary

**Every `*ErrorKind` / `LimitKind` / json `ParseError` / path `ResolveError` / protocol enum is exhaustive `pub(all)`** — adding a variant after 1.0 breaks user `match`. Only 4 enums in core use `#non_exhaustive`. Proposal: `#non_exhaustive` on all of them now. [cross-package:27]

## Context from the review

Copied from the batch report (evidence, reproduction, proposed fix). `Source: codex` means the finding came from the Codex pass and was re-verified by the reviewer.

### cross-package-2 — Error-kind and protocol enums are exhaustive `pub(all)`; `#non_exhaustive` used on only 4 enums
_High · API · breaking to fix: yes (only if done after 1.0) · from the [`cross-package` report](https://github.com/moonbitlang/core/issues/4612#issuecomment-6620751625)_

- where: `pub(all) enum` without `#non_exhaustive`: `ZipErrorKind`(15 variants) `LimitKind`(6) `Compression` (archive/zip), `InflateErrorKind`(6) `Strategy` `Status` `DeflateAction` `InputMode` (compress/flate), `GzipErrorKind`(8), `ZlibErrorKind`(10), `json.ParseError`(6, `pub(all) suberror`), `path/error.ResolveError`(1!), `async/fs.FsEvent` `CreateMode` `SyncMode` `Mode`, `async/shell.Redirect` `Stdin`, `async/signal.Signal`, `async/websocket.CloseCode`(11) `MessageKind`, `async/http.RequestMethod`(10) `Protocol`, `async/tls.TrustedRoot` `X509FileType`, `async/types.Platform`, `async/socket.IpProtocolPreference`, `async.RetryMethod`, `argparse.FlagAction` `ParseOutcome`. The only `#non_exhaustive` enums in core: `async/os_error.Kind`, `async/fs.FileKind`, `async/process.ProcessInput`/`ProcessOutput` (`async/os_error/error_kind.mbt:19`, `async/fs/constants.mbt:18`, `async/process/redirect.mbt:162,252`).
- what: an error-kind enum *will* grow (new limit kinds, new header errors; `ResolveError` has a single variant today). Without `#non_exhaustive`, every exhaustive user `match` breaks when a variant is added. `pub(all)` additionally lets users construct `GzipErrorKind::Truncated` etc., which is harmless but freezes payload shapes (`OutputLimitExceeded(limit~ : UInt64, observed~ : UInt64)`).
- fix: add `#non_exhaustive` to every `*ErrorKind`, `LimitKind`, `ParseError`, `ResolveError`, `FsEvent`, `Signal`, `CloseCode`, `RequestMethod`, `Platform`, `Redirect`, `Stdin`, `Strategy`. Keep exhaustive only for genuinely closed sets (`Lock`, `Mode`, `InputMode`, `Compression`? — decide). Rule for the style guide below.
- Source: both (codex flagged the 4 compress/zip kinds; full list is mine).
